They need reconciling: the driver's real cost is the deadhead time and fuel back, plus tolls on voluntary repositioning only.

Airport-queue duplicates: R01-052, R05-063, R06-040, R06-041 and R02-049 all describe the same queue state, and R01-053 and R09-057 are the same join/stay/leave decision. Merge them into one state and one decision. R06-040's 'one FIFO per airport and platform' is probably wrong, because app queues appear to be separate per product.

The airport queue is spread over five items that describe one queue object: R01-052, R02-049, R05-063, R06-040 and R06-041, plus R06-045 (service rate). Merge them into one state, one rule set (R06-042 to R06-044) and one agent decision.

Clusters that repeat one setting 3-5 times: platform lockouts (R02-059, R06-054, R07-030, R09-042); passenger-time cap (R02-060, R07-047, R09-005); offer information shown before accepting (R05-036, R06-025, R07-041, all rated high); data era (R02-033, R05-005, R10-064, R12-043, plus R07-065 rule vintage); taxi lease (R02-045, R07-016, R08-042, R09-003).

The central with/without-information experiment is defined in several places, which risks the arms drifting apart: event info in R03-060, R12-008 and R12-016 (plus R03-061 feeds); weather info in R04-049, R04-050 and R12-015; incident latency in R03-062, R10-028 and R12-017; alerts in R04-051. These should be sub-items of the single information ladder R12-013.

Event and traffic objects are duplicated across dossiers: R03-044 vs R04-016 (emergencies and travel bans); R03-043 vs R04-029 (power outages); R03-045 vs R06-051 (platform outage); R03-038 vs R10-025 (crashes); R03-052 vs R10-024 (overnight closures); R03-029 to R03-037 vs R10-026 and R10-027 (planned and VIP closures); R01-013 and R01-014 vs R10-015 (one-way and turn rules); R01-028 and R01-029 vs R10-017 and R10-018 (busways, car-free streets); R01-016 vs R10-030 to R10-032 (cameras); R02-063 vs R04-035 (daylight).

Conflicting impact ratings and evidence for the same mechanism. R10-006 (weather-to-speed coupling) is rated low because a TLC check found no daily slowdown, while R04-008 (weather speed-penalty table) is rated high on DOT sensor ratios of 0.91 for heavy rain and 0.51 for heavy snow. Reconcile them into one item, probably medium (snow matters, rain little). Likewise R04-037 (high) vs R08-010 (medium) for EV range loss in the cold: R04-037's own note says the -41% figure is an extreme seen on about 15 days a year, so 'high' looks overstated.

Items filed under the wrong component. The agent decisions R03-057, R03-058 and R03-059 are under 'Benchmark harness', while every other agent action (R09-052 to R09-070) is under 'Driver state'. R12-059 is a scoring panel but has role 'rule' under 'Regulation, fees & taxes'. R01-069 (safety and crime, under 'Competitor supply & matching') duplicates R09-031 (under 'Events & disruptions').

R12-052, the operations-research planner baseline, 'reads the generator's expected rates'. Under R12-021 that is insider information, since models see only public history, so the baseline is not on an equal information footing. problems: The airport queue is one object listed five times: R01-052, R02-049, R05-063, R06-040 and R06-041 all describe queue length or wait. The same agent decision also appears twice (R01-053, R09-057). Merge them into one queue state and one decision, and keep R06-042, R06-043 and R07-051 as the rules.

The hours cap and lockouts are listed several times and the wording has drifted apart. Passenger-time cap: R02-060 = R07-047 = R09-005 (R07-047 says itself that it duplicates R09-005). Platform lockouts: R02-059 = R06-054 = R07-030 = R09-042, each summarising the rule history differently. Destination filter: R06-028 = R09-017, and they disagree on Lyft's limit (6 a day vs 2-6 a day).

Exact duplicates: driver home location R01-061 = R09-015; taxi 4-5 pm shift change R02-044 = R06-018; taxi overnight surcharge R02-054 = R07-004; weekday rush surcharge R02-055 = R07-003; cruising cap R06-055 = R07-032, which disagree on whether the rule was annulled or is 'still printed'.

The robotaxi operating domain is split across six variables with different roles and components: R01-008 (setting, Map), R07-060 (rule, Regulation), R06-058 (rule, Vehicle), R02-061 (setting, Fleet manager), R04-039 (rule, Fleet manager) and R10-023 (rule, Traffic). None of them says whether both trip ends must be inside the area. Make one ODD object (polygon, hours, road classes, crossings, weather limits, endpoint rule) with these as its attributes.

The same fleet quantity is listed twice in several places. R09-044 duty cycle (20-22 h a day) vs R11-042 availability: the R11 fact-check corrected 75% to 83-92%, but R09-044 was not updated. R06-062 own-fleet cannibalisation vs R11-030 saturation curve: both describe the same N vs N+dN test. Also R05-068 vs R11-057 (induced demand), R09-049 vs R11-052 (remote-assistance staffing), and R01-063 / R09-045 / R11-043 / R08-064 (depots).

Robotaxi operations items overlap: vandalism appears in R03-056, R08-059 and R11-063; sensor cleaning in R04-040 and R08-062; cabin mess in R04-042, R05-054 and R09-046 (plus the cleaning schedule R09-047). Merge them into one damage-and-obstruction hazard and one cabin-state machine so downtime is not counted twice.

Many entries are simulation outputs, not inputs: R06-035 ping rate, R06-036 utilisation, R06-037 idle gap, R10-051 cruising share, R11-022 empty miles, R11-028 clustering, R11-030 saturation, R11-041 share charging at peaks, R11-042 availability, R11-064 profit variance, and R06-057 robotaxi trips per car-day (which is even tagged 'world'). Move them to a 'calibration targets / KPIs' box so nobody sets them as inputs.

R11-056 and R06-061 judge market impact by citywide share ('negligible below 100 cars, under 1% of supply'). But surge and pickup ETAs are set per zone. A stack of 30-50 cars at a venue or airport (R11-024, R11-025) can be most of the idle supply in that zone, so price impact and self-cannibalisation show up even with a small fleet. Impact should be judged per zone and hour.

Impact ratings conflict for the same mechanism. R04-008 rates the weather speed table 'high' (heavy snow x0.51), while R10-006 rates weather-to-speed coupling 'low' and says no daily slowdown was found. For the robotaxi track, R09-048 rates the remote-assistance rate 'low', yet its own figure (one session every 2.5-5 mi) means several sessions per car-hour in Manhattan, and it feeds two 'medium' items (R09-049, R11-052). R01-033 rates robotaxi pickup-point placement 'low' although it is the main AV pickup penalty in Midtown. Both should be medium for robotaxis.

R11-030 assumes revenue per car falls steadily as N grows. In own-app mode, the fleet's own density sets its pickup ETAs (roughly with the square root of idle-car density), so with a small fleet each extra car can raise profit per car before saturation sets in. The N ladder {1, 10, 100} in R11-067 may miss that rise, so add intermediate N values.

gap_vars.sub_box: R07 Pricing, platform and regulation / D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor

Pay exceeds the fare on 10.3% of Uber and 5.9% of Lyft trips, mostly where the NYC per-mile and per-minute floor binds [design interpretation]. Variance of the ratio: platform alone explains <1%; adding the OD pair explains about 8%; within platform x OD x 4-hour band (cells >= 20 trips), 90% remains. Within those cells (>= 30 trips, median 2-6 mi), per-mile pay p90/p10 = 1.60, median $3.88/mi. Daniel Abayev and Peter Leyman of Queens worked with two Russian hackers to charge yellow-cab drivers $10 to skip the JFK taxi-hold line, sending up to about 1,000 taxis a day to the front. Both pleaded guilty in Oct 2023 and were sentenced to 4 and 2 years. [S] NBC NY airport-queue bribery case (R01-052). Detection rates are [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; taxi; fleet of human-driven cars
gap_vars.data_source: DOJ SDNY sentencing release https://www.justice.gov/usao-sdny/pr/queens-men-sentenced-prison-conspiring-hack-taxi-dispatch-system-jfk-airport ; 35 RCNY penalty tables via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive
gap_vars.how_to_model: Optional illegal actions, each with an expected gain, a detection draw per act, and the fine or deactivation from R07. Scored in the compliance panel (R12-059) and reported as a cheating rate.

gap_vars.sub_box: R08 Vehicle and costs / Tolls, parking and fines paid by the driver
gap_vars.name: Towing, impound and hearing time
gap_vars.description: Rare, costly events that cost both money and shift hours: a tow from a no-standing, hydrant or rush-hour lane spot, getting the car back from the impound lot, and time spent contesting summonses. Fees are NYC-specific; generalise with a city fee table.
gap_vars.values_or_range: NYPD tow for a parking or standing violation: $185 regular ($370 heavy duty) plus $20 per night of storage, on top of the ticket. Booted cars follow a separate Department of Finance schedule: a car is booted once it owes >= $350 in judgment tickets, and towed if not paid within 48 h. For cars booted on or after 1 Nov 2025, the boot fee rises from $142 to $185 and the tow (< 8,500 lb) from $140 to $220. Storage rises from $10/day (first 3 days) then $15, to $30/day then $50. A 5% poundage fee is added. Reaching the pound and paying takes 2-4 h [design]. Each summons hearing takes 1-4 h (OATH for TLC; DOF for parking; DMV TVB for moving violations) [design]. Tow hazard: 0-0.5 per 1,000 h parked at illegal Midtown curbs [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] NYPD towed-vehicles page, NYC DOF towed-vehicle FAQ and nyc.gov/booting via search snippets; the fee tables were not read directly. [corrected: '$140-220 tow, $30/$50 storage' are the old and new DOF boot-and-tow fees, not a range, and do not apply to NYPD tows]. Time losses are [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; taxi (robotaxi depots rarely street-park)
gap_vars.data_source: NYPD towed vehicles https://www.nyc.gov/site/nypd/services/vehicles-property/towed-vehicles.page ; NYC DOF FAQ https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/vehicles/services-towed-vehicles-faq.page ; DOF booting https://www.nyc.gov/booting ; NYC Open Data parking violations (hazard by street)
gap_vars.how_to_model: When the agent waits or parks at an illegal curb (R01-025), draw a tow with a hazard by street class and hour. A tow costs fee + storage + 2-4 h off-shift. Each summons can be contested through an optional hearing action that costs time and may cut the fine (ledger in R08-053).

gap_vars.sub_box: R02 Time patterns / B. Hour-of-day demand profile
gap_vars.name: Minute-of-hour request pulses
gap_vars.description: Ride requests bunch slightly at round clock times (on the hour, the half hour, and 10 or 40 past) as meetings, classes and shows end on the clock.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023, non-holiday weekdays, requests 07-20h. Midtown/Penn zones (100, 161-164, 186, 230), on-demand requests (wait <= 15 min): minute :10 is 1.15x the mean, :40 1.14x, :30 1.10x, :00 1.09x, :55 1.08x; trough 0.93-0.94x at :19-:23. Citywide (8.4M requests): peaks are 1.06-1.12x (at :40, :10, :45, :15, :30 and :00), and 5-minute block averages stay within about +/-3% (0.98-1.03). Airports peak at :55-:59 (1.04-1.06x). Pickup minutes are almost flat (+/-6%).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on HVFHV Jan 2023 request_datetime (g1/a1.py, a2.py), re-run in this fact-check, with 5-minute blocks added. [corrected: pickup minutes +/-6%, not +/-5%]. Median waits are slightly shorter at the peak minutes (3.35-3.43 vs 3.65 min), so the peaks are not just scheduled reservations.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime to the second)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Optional periodic term on each zone's arrival rate (minute weights per zone class). It matters only with 1-minute ticks (R02-067).

gap_vars.sub_box: R02 Time patterns / E. Month, season and year
gap_vars.name: Summer recreation destinations
gap_vars.description: Warm-weather trips to beaches and parks (Rockaway, Coney Island, Orchard Beach) and out-of-town getaways pull cars to dead-end peninsulas where return trips are scarce. The zones are NYC-specific; any coastal city has an equivalent.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Yellow 2023 drop-offs into the Rockaway zones (27, 86, 117, 201): about 49/day in Jun-Aug vs 36/day in January (+35%). October also reaches 46/day, so part of the rise is a broad Apr-Oct season rather than beach days. Coney Island (55): 21/day in Jul-Aug vs 14 in January (+50%). Summer yellow pickups per drop-off: only 0.24 in Rockaway and 0.32 in Coney Island. The effect is likely concentrated on hot, dry weekends [U].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on TLC yellow 2023 drop-offs by zone and month, re-run in this fact-check. September is depressed by the 21-24 Sep 2023 data gap (R02-065). Volumes are small (tens of yellow trips a day). App trips, which dominate outer-borough demand, are not measured.
gap_vars.applies_to: all; single car (stranding risk), fleet (rebalancing out)
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page ; NOAA hourly weather; NYC Parks beach attendance (no machine-readable source found)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Season x temperature x weekend multiplier on drop-offs to beach zones. The low pickup rate there feeds destination re-dispatch value (R05-058).

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / D. Price, wait and mode choice
gap_vars.name: Transit alternatives to the airports
gap_vars.description: The price and reliability of rail and bus links to JFK, LGA and EWR, which cap how many travellers take a car and how sharply that share falls when surge is high. Generalises to any city with airport rail or bus links.
gap_vars.values_or_range: AirTrain JFK costs $8.50, plus subway or LIRR. It was half price ($4.25) from 30 Jun to Labor Day (1 Sep) 2025 at Jamaica and Howard Beach, as also in summer 2024. AirTrain JFK carried about 11.7M riders in 2025 (6.7M in 2023), about 30.7k per weekday in Q1 2026. The Q70 LaGuardia Link has been fare-free since 1 May 2022; its 2024 ridership was about 25% above 2019. EWR: AirTrain Newark plus NJ Transit or Amtrak. Outages are in R03-049.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] NY1, Frommers and 6sqft (Jun 2025) on the half-price AirTrain. [S] The Points Guy (1 May 2022) and an MTA service document on the fare-free Q70. [S] AirTrain ridership via Wikipedia only; the PANYNJ figure was not read.
gap_vars.data_source: PANYNJ airport traffic reports https://www.panynj.gov/airports/en/statistics-general-info.html ; MTA ridership (data.ny.gov); MTA airport guides https://www.mta.info/guides/airports/laguardia
gap_vars.how_to_model: Airport-trip mode choice (nested logit on fare, time, luggage and hour). Transit fares are rule inputs, with scenario toggles for fare changes or outages.

gap_vars.sub_box: R09 Driver (human) / J. Agent decisions (action space)
gap_vars.name: App controls: pause, last trip, auto-accept, filter to any place
gap_vars.description: Driver-app controls beyond accept and decline: pausing or going offline, blocking back-to-back requests before the last trip, and auto-accept where offered. Aiming the destination filter at any place (for example JFK) is covered by R09-017 and R06-028.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Actions: pause/offline; a 'stop new requests' or 'last ride' flag; auto-accept on/off (availability varies by market [U]); destination-filter target = any zone, with Uber's 2 uses/day (R09-017). Back-to-back requests are on by default and cannot be switched off. Uber's pages show a stop-requests (hand) button in the delivery app, and for rides they say to tap 'Go Offline' in the Trip Planner.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Uber help pages on back-to-back trips via snippets (uber.com unreachable). Delivery variants are in English; the ride variant was seen only in Russian. [corrected: going offline is not the only documented way to stop requests]. Forum reports of a ride-side 'stop new requests' button [S, anecdotal]. Auto-accept is [U].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; fleet of app cars
gap_vars.data_source: Uber back-to-back help pages: delivery https://www.uber.com/drive/delivery/basics/back-to-back-trips/ ; ride variant e.g. https://www.uber.com/lt/ru/drive/basics/back-to-back-trips/ [uncertain: a US English ride page was not confirmed]; none found for usage rates
gap_vars.how_to_model: Action flags in the agent API. Forward dispatch (R06-023) skips agents with the last-trip flag set. The filter target accepts any zone (mechanics in R09-017).

gap_vars.sub_box: R07 Pricing, platform and regulation / E. Incentives, fees and pass-throughs
gap_vars.name: Driver-side pay errors and support claims
gap_vars.description: Small pay errors that go against the driver, such as a missing toll reimbursement, unpaid wait time or cancellation fee, or distance cut short by GPS drift. A driver recovers them only partly, by filing support tickets. This is distinct from rider disputes (R05-056) and the toll rule itself (R07-038).
gap_vars.values_or_range: Error rate 0.5-3% of trips; $2-15 per error; 30-80% recovered if claimed; 5-15 min of unpaid time per claim [design guess].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [U] Driver-forum reports; [design]. Not checkable with public data.
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver (taxi meter errors are rare)
gap_vars.data_source: none found
gap_vars.how_to_model: Bernoulli error per trip on the toll, wait-fee and cancel-fee components. The agent can file a claim, which costs time and succeeds with a recovery probability.

gap_vars.sub_box: R06 Supply and competition / A. Background supply volume and mix
gap_vars.name: Informal and unlicensed competition
gap_vars.description: Dollar vans, unlicensed livery cars and illegal street pickups by app cars, which take cheap short trips and hails in some neighbourhoods and at let-outs. Informal transit exists in other cities too, but its size is local.
gap_vars.values_or_range: TLC chair (Oct 2024): 35 TLC-licensed commuter vans vs 215 in 2019. Other counts: 31 in service (THE CITY); 38 licensed vehicles at 12 bases (City Council, 2024); 584 licensed in 2015. A state insurance-subsidy programme from Sep 2024 was credited with a 50% rise in licensed vans. Many more unlicensed vans run on the Flatbush Ave, Jamaica and Chinatown corridors [U]. Ridership is about 120,000/day (King & Goldwyn 2014 estimate; about 125,000 in a recent Economist piece) [S, dated]. Demand lost: 0-10% of short trips in affected zones [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] City Limits and Next City (TLC chair, Oct 2024); amNY (City Council 2024 counts); ridership via an ASU study citing King & Goldwyn 2014. No current official ridership count exists. [corrected: ridership '~100k+ [U]' replaced by dated estimates].
gap_vars.data_source: TLC commuter-van licensing (counts via press); none found for unlicensed activity
gap_vars.how_to_model: Remove a zone-hour share of short-trip and hail demand before generation. Illegal hail competitors at let-outs reduce taxi hail encounters (R05-042).

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / E. Request attributes and special needs
gap_vars.name: Service animals and other riders who must be carried
gap_vars.description: Riders with service animals or folded mobility devices must be carried; refusing them counts as a service refusal, with fines and possible loss of the licence or app account. The ADA gives a similar duty across the US.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0.1-0.5% of requests come with a service animal [design guess]. Refusing one is a service refusal. For taxis the penalty is $350 / $500 (pleaded / after hearing) for a first offence, rising to $750 / $1,000 plus licence revocation for a third within 36 months (35 RCNY 80-20, R07-042). App deactivation risk [U]. The animal is not revealed until pickup.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] TLC Industry Notice 10-28 (29 Nov 2010, repeating 09-23): service animals must be admitted in all taxis and FHVs, secured or not; refusal is a service refusal, with penalties up to licence suspension or revocation. A Dec 2020 TLC amendment updated the service-animal wording [S]. [P*, from list] penalty table in R07-042. [U] ADA 49 CFR 37.167(d). [corrected: dated '$300-1,000' fines replaced by the current penalty table].
gap_vars.applies_to: all (a robotaxi must carry them too)
gap_vars.data_source: TLC Industry Notice 10-28 https://www.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/archived_industry_notices/industry_notice_10_28.pdf ; 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive
gap_vars.how_to_model: Request flag revealed at pickup. Refusal triggers a fine or deactivation draw (R07-042) and a compliance-panel entry (R12-059).

gap_vars.sub_box: R01 Geography and network / Road network structure
gap_vars.name: Gated and single-access destinations
gap_vars.description: Destinations behind gates or ID checks, or reachable by only one road, add a security wait or a long detour that a zone-level map misses. The examples are NYC places; other cities can be generalised from OSM tags.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Brooklyn Navy Yard (gated); Fort Hamilton (military ID check); Rikers Island (single bridge, security); Breezy Point (gated private cooperative); Roosevelt Island (cars only via the bridge from Queens); City Island (single bridge); JFK cargo areas. Gate delay 2-15 min. Detour up to 10-20 min, e.g. reaching Roosevelt Island from Manhattan [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [U] Local geography; [design]. Could be measured from OSM barrier and access tags.
gap_vars.data_source: OpenStreetMap (barrier=gate, access=private/permissive) https://www.openstreetmap.org
gap_vars.how_to_model: Gate nodes with a delay distribution and an access class per vehicle type. Single-access zones are routed only through their one link.

gap_vars.sub_box: R04 Weather / Snow, ice and winter roads
gap_vars.name: Digging out after a storm
gap_vars.description: Street-parked cars get plowed in after snow, so drivers lose 30-90 minutes clearing the car before the first trip on high-demand snow days.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Delay of 30-90 min after >= 4 in of snow for street-parked cars; about 0 for garaged cars and depot fleets [design]. NYC suspends alternate-side parking during snow operations, while parking meters stay in force.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]; [S] 311 and press (PIX11, Newsweek) on alternate-side parking suspensions for snow operations.
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; taxi (garages and robotaxi depots exempt)
gap_vars.data_source: NOAA GHCN-Daily snowfall (Central Park USW00094728); NYC 311 alternate-side parking status
gap_vars.how_to_model: Draw a shift-start delay when overnight snowfall passes a threshold, depending on parking type (R08-052).

gap_vars.sub_box: R10 Traffic and travel time / Curb, pickup and drop-off
gap_vars.name: Night garbage-truck blockages
gap_vars.description: Private carters and city sanitation trucks stop on narrow streets, mostly 22:00-06:00, and hold up traffic for minutes on one-lane streets. Daytime delivery blockage is R10-038. The Commercial Waste Zones are NYC-specific; night refuse blockage generalises.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 1-5 min per encounter; 2-10% chance per late-night trip on one-lane Manhattan and Brooklyn streets [design]. Commercial Waste Zones: 20 zones. The first (Queens Central) moved over between 3 Sep 2024 and 2 Jan 2025, with contracts with a zone carter required from 3 Jan 2025. The Bronx zones followed in late 2025, and Lower Manhattan sign-up opened on 1 Apr 2026. Full rollout is expected by the end of 2027 [S]. Fewer private trucks per street should follow [U].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] DSNY CWZ rule and rollout-schedule pages via search snippets. [corrected: first-zone dates]. [uncertain: the claim 'about half of zones by Dec 2026' was not found]. Night timing [U]; delays [design].
gap_vars.data_source: DSNY Commercial Waste Zones https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/resources/reports/commercial-waste-zones-plan.page ; rollout schedule https://www.nyc.gov/site/dsny/businesses/cwz/rollout-schedule.page ; DSNY collection schedules (NYC Open Data) [U]
gap_vars.how_to_model: Blocking hazard on local one-lane edges by hour. It is absorbed in calibrated night speeds unless traffic is modelled at link level.

gap_vars.sub_box: R01 Geography and network / Curb access and restricted streets
gap_vars.name: Doorman and hotel-starter relationships
gap_vars.description: Doormen and hotel starters may steer the best fares, such as airport runs, to cabs or black cars they know, sometimes for a tip.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0-20% of hotel-stand airport fares steered to 'regular' drivers [design]; $5-20 tip to the starter [U].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [U] Industry lore and press; no data found.
gap_vars.applies_to: taxi; human black-car driver (not app pool, not robotaxi)
gap_vars.data_source: none found
gap_vars.how_to_model: At hotel stands (R05-044), a 'regular' state, built by repeat visits and tips, raises the chance of getting a long fare.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / A. Trip generation volume (effect composition)
gap_vars.name: Modifier composition and saturation rule
gap_vars.description: How base demand and the hour, day-type, weather, event, holiday and transit-disruption effects are combined (multiplied, added or fitted jointly), and where combined demand is capped.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Modes: (1) product of separately fitted multipliers; (2) one joint negative-binomial GLM on zone x 15-min counts, with main effects plus selected interactions (rain x hour, event x weather, holiday x hour); (3) additive event residual on a multiplicative base. Cap per zone-hour at an observed ceiling (max 1,625 HVFHV pickups per zone-hour, R05-001) or a surge-implied ceiling.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design guess] Stacked days (rain + event + holiday) are likely the most profitable scenarios, so the stacking rule sets the biggest payoffs. [P, from list] R04-002 plans a Poisson regression with hour-of-week fixed effects; its only fitted result so far is a daily wet-day regression (Uber +6.3%). [corrected: it was described as already fitted hourly].
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records; NOAA hourly weather (LCD); event calendar (R03)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Fit one log-link GLM jointly and validate it on held-out stacked days. Apply the ceiling as a soft cap, and record the composition rule used in each scenario.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / J. Latent demand and demand feedback
gap_vars.name: Supply-constrained bias in fitted weather and event effects
gap_vars.description: Rain, event and holiday uplifts estimated from completed trips understate the real jump in requests, because extra requests in busy hours are capped by the cars available. This applies the censoring in R05-066 to effect estimates; merge candidate with R05-066.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Correction factor 1.0-1.5x on fitted uplifts in tight hours [design]. Diagnostic (HVFHV Jan 2023, 20 non-holiday weekdays): daily trips vs median request-to-pickup wait r = +0.62 raw and +0.81 after removing day-of-week means, so busier days are tighter.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Re-run in this fact-check (g1/a7.py plus a de-meaned check): raw 0.62, de-meaned 0.81 (the gap critic had 0.80). Part of the correlation is the post-holiday ramp within January. [S] Brodeur & Nield, IZA DP 9986 (2016) and JEBO 152 (2018): Uber rides per hour about 25% higher in rain vs about 4% for taxis, explained by surge-induced supply. A 2017 working-paper version with Uber data to Dec 2016 reports about 18% vs 5%. [uncertain: which pair the JEBO article reports; snippets conflict and iza.org was unreachable].
gap_vars.data_source: HVFHV request, on-scene and pickup times; NOAA hourly weather
gap_vars.how_to_model: Estimate uplifts with wait-adjusted or censored (Tobit-style) regressions, or back out requests by inverting the sim's matcher. Cross-link R05-066.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / D. Price, wait and mode choice
gap_vars.name: Pre-match abandonment and 'no cars available'
gap_vars.description: How long a rider keeps waiting while the app is still searching for a car, and the platform rule that refuses or hides service when no car is within an ETA threshold. This is pre-match; post-match cancels are R05-022.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Search patience: median 1-3 min, then the rider abandons or switches app or mode [design]. 'No cars available' when the best ETA exceeds 15-25 min [design]. Abandonment 0-10% of requests citywide, far higher at night in outer zones [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] Castillo, Knoepfle & Weyl: in thin hours and areas, riders cancel and waits jump (R06-039). TLC records hold completed trips only, so no public abandonment rate exists.
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; robotaxi; fleet; taxi e-hail
gap_vars.data_source: none found (unmatched requests are not published)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Each unmatched request draws a patience time. It leaves (to a rival, to a taxi hail, or lost) when patience runs out or the platform ETA threshold is exceeded. Feeds R06-022 and R06-039.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / D. Price, wait and mode choice
gap_vars.name: Riders moving out of surge zones
gap_vars.description: When surge or ETA is high, some riders walk to a cheaper or better-served neighbouring zone, or move the pickup pin, so demand leaks across surge boundaries.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0-15% of surge-exposed requests move 100-400 m [design]; no NYC estimate found.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]; [U] rider walking is widely reported, but no NYC estimate was found.
gap_vars.data_source: none found
gap_vars.how_to_model: For requests facing surge above a threshold, move the origin with probability p to an adjacent zone with lower surge or ETA, and add walk time.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Data pipeline and calibration
gap_vars.name: Sparse cells and smoothing of rates
gap_vars.description: How rate tables estimated from few observations (outer-zone x 15-min demand, pay ratios, travel times) are smoothed, so that noise does not create fake hotspots that the agent learns.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023, 20 non-holiday weekdays: 11.3% of zone x hour cells average under 5 trips/h and 5.4% under 1 (counting all 263 zones; 10.6% and 4.7% over the 261 zones with any trip). 48.6% of the ~55.6k observed OD pairs average under 1 trip/day. Methods: empirical-Bayes pooling toward borough-hour means, neighbour averaging, gravity fallback. OD smoothing is already in R05-006; R10-062 uses OD neighbour averaging for travel times.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Re-run in this fact-check on the local HVFHV file (55,618 OD pairs vs the critic's 55,974; shares agree within 0.1 point). [P, from list] R05-006 (Bayesian OD smoothing) and R10-062 (neighbour averaging of travel times).
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
gap_vars.how_to_model: Shrinkage estimator per table, with a documented prior and strength. Test that a model with memory gains nothing from cells that smoothing removes.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Scenarios, seeds, difficulty and leakage (randomness and correlation)
gap_vars.name: Shared day-level shock across modules
gap_vars.description: One hidden day-and-area factor that moves demand, travel speed, rider waits and surge together, instead of separate random draws in each module. It couples R05-002 (demand overdispersion) and R10-009 (day-level slowdowns).
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023, 20 non-holiday weekdays, day-of-week means removed: trips vs median wait r = +0.81; trips vs Manhattan-internal speed r = -0.86; wait vs speed r = -0.86 (raw: +0.62, -0.68, -0.79). Modes: independent draws / one shared factor with a loading per module / Gaussian copula.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Re-run in this fact-check: all six correlations reproduced within 0.01 (speed = Manhattan-internal miles / trip time). Only 20 days are used, and part of the correlation is the post-holiday ramp within January (trips rose from 478k on 3 Jan to 701k on 27 Jan); validate on more months. [corrected: impact high -> medium. R12-040 finds pay per engaged hour varies only 1.4% across these days, so the shock moves volume, waits and variance more than profit per hour. Its effect on profit per online hour is unmeasured].
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV records; NYC DOT Traffic Speeds https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/i4gi-tjb9
gap_vars.how_to_model: Draw a latent daily factor z ~ N(0,1) per area: demand x exp(a z), speed x exp(-b z), bot log-on x exp(c z). Fit the loadings on several months, and seed z in the common-random-number stream (R12-040).

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Baselines and scoring
gap_vars.name: Jackpot-trip variance and luck-adjusted scoring
gap_vars.description: How the score handles rare high-value trips that dominate a single day's profit, for example by subtracting a baseline run on the same seed (control variate) or by scoring the expected value of the trips offered.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023: the top 1% of trips by driver pay (>= $68.72) earn 5.5% of all pay; the top 5% (>= $43.04) earn 17.7%; 0.27% of trips pay >= $100; 91% of top-1% trips touch an airport or leave NYC. Mean pay is $17.05 per trip (median $12.81), so at ~20-25 trips a day one $100 trip is about 23-29% of daily pay. Methods: none / paired baseline on the same seed / control variate on offered-trip value / both.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own re-run on HVFHV Jan 2023 (18.19M trips with pay; g1/a7.py), repeated in this fact-check. [corrected: share of daily pay was 15-25%]. Trips per day [U]. [U] Control variates are standard (Law & Kelton).
gap_vars.applies_to: all; matters most for single-car runs (a fleet averages over N cars)
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV records (driver_pay)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Log the value of every offered trip. Score = profit - beta x (offered jackpot value - its expectation), with beta fitted across runs. Report raw and adjusted scores.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Observation, actions and decision cadence
gap_vars.name: Within-step update order
gap_vars.description: The fixed order in which request arrivals, surge updates, batch matching, bot moves, agent actions and state updates run when events share a timestamp.
gap_vars.values_or_range: A fixed, documented order, e.g. arrivals -> surge computed from the pre-match state -> matching -> bots -> agent -> state. Ties broken by a seeded random draw or by entity id. Sensitivity test with 2-3 alternative orders [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] R12-026 specifies a SimPy-style priority queue but no ordering for events with the same timestamp.
gap_vars.data_source: none needed
gap_vars.how_to_model: Priority classes in the event queue; a unit test that results do not depend on container order; report the score change under alternative orders.

gap_vars.sub_box: R06 Supply and competition / C. Platform dispatch and matching
gap_vars.name: Equal dispatch treatment of agent and background cars
gap_vars.description: Whether the simulated matcher, offer timeout, dispatch radius, tier perks and penalties treat the agent's cars exactly like the background bots.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Parity (default) / documented deviations. Checks: the agent's share of offers vs bots at equal ETA, decline-cascade timing, and tier perks (R09-041) applied by state, not by identity [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]. [S, from list] Real apps have priority tiers (Uber Pro, R09-041), so any perk must be applied the same way to both.
gap_vars.data_source: none needed

gap_vars.sub_box: R06 Supply and competition / B. Competitor driver behaviour
gap_vars.name: Competitor information level as its own setting
gap_vars.description: How much public event, weather and calendar information the background bots act on (share of informed bots and their lead time), set separately from the agent's information arm.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Share of informed bots 0 / 25 / 50 / 100%; lead time 0-120 min; crossed with the agent's arm (R03-060, R04-049) in a 2x2 or 3x2 design [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P, from list] R06-052 ties bot event knowledge to the agent's treatment arm, which mixes two effects into one; [design].
gap_vars.data_source: none needed
gap_vars.how_to_model: The bot policy reads the same info feeds through a per-bot access flag. The experiment matrix crosses bot and agent information levels.

gap_vars.sub_box: R07 Pricing, platform and regulation / C. App rider fares, surge and taxes
gap_vars.name: Surge frequency calibration target
gap_vars.description: How often, when and how strongly app prices rise above normal, estimated from public trip fares and used to calibrate the surge module.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023 weekdays, non-shared trips of normal duration (<= 1.1x the OD median time): 6.9-7.8% priced >= 1.3x the median fare for the same platform and OD pair, and 2.6-3.0% >= 1.6x (the range covers two filters). By request hour: 12.4-13.0% at 07-08h, 8.4-9.0% at 17-18h, 3.2-3.9% at 02-04h (our re-check vs the critic). Drivers get a lower share of surged fares (median pay/fare 0.67-0.68 vs 0.72).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own calc (g1/a2.py), re-run in this fact-check, plus an hourly re-check with holidays excluded; it agrees with the gap critic within 1 point. This is a proxy: the duration filter keeps faster-than-median trips, and the fare ratio includes upfront-price noise and route differences.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV records (base_passenger_fare by OD and time)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Tune surge thresholds (R07-020) until the simulated distribution of fare ratios by hour matches the target. Calibration fails if it is off by more than a set number of percentage points.

gap_vars.sub_box: R10 Traffic and travel time / Travel-time engine and calibration
gap_vars.name: Routed vs recorded distance ratio
gap_vars.description: The gap between the router's shortest-path distance and the distance real trips record for the same OD pair and hour. It scales fares, the per-mile pay floor and energy cost.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023, OD x 4-hour cells (>= 200 trips, median >= 3 mi; 7,190 cells): median trip_miles is 1.20x the 10th percentile and 1.27x the 5th; p90/p10 = 1.52 (includes address spread within zones). Yellow trips are about 4% shorter than app trips on the same OD: median ratio 0.96 (IQR 0.93-0.99) over 2,199 OD pairs; trip-weighted 0.98. The router-vs-record ratio still needs to be measured with an OSM router.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on HVFHV and yellow Jan 2023 (g1/a6.py), re-run in this fact-check. Part of the taxi-app gap may come from different odometers (taximeter vs app GPS) [U]. Router comparison [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: all (separate factors for taxi and app)
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records (trip_miles, trip_distance); OpenStreetMap with OSRM or Valhalla
gap_vars.how_to_model: Detour factor per OD-hour = recorded median / routed distance, applied to paid distance and energy, separately for taxi and app. Validate on a held-out month.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Data pipeline and calibration
gap_vars.name: Back-tests on real policy changes and shocks
gap_vars.description: Checks that the sim, calibrated on data from before a real policy change or shock, reproduces the change observed after it.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Candidate tests: the CBD toll from 5 Jan 2025 (speeds and trips, R10-005); HVFHV lockout rules (R07-030); the distance-factor reset on 13 Mar 2023 (R07-028); storms such as 29 Sep 2023 (R04-025). Pass if the predicted change is within +/-30-50% of the observed one [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P, from list] Congestion-pricing speed regime (R10-005); yellow trips +19% from 2024 to 2025 (R02-033); [design].
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records before and after each change; NYC DOT traffic speeds; MTA CBD toll data (data.ny.gov)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Calibrate on the pre-period, switch the rule or shock on, and compare simulated vs observed changes in trips, speeds, waits and pay.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
gap_vars.name: What state carries over between days
gap_vars.description: Which physical and account states persist from days 1-10 into day 11: car position, fuel or charge, rating, acceptance and cancellation rates, weekly quest progress, weekly lease, weekly hours used and fatigue.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Options: reset everything daily / carry position and energy / carry account standing / carry everything (default for the learning test) [design]. Weekly items: quests (R07-033), leases (R02-045), and the TLC passenger-time cap of 10 h per 24 h and 60 h per week (R09-005).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S, from list] Weekly quests, leases and hour caps; [design]. R12-033 covers memory notes only. [corrected: the TLC cap counts passenger time only].

gap_vars.how_to_model: State snapshot at each day boundary, with a carry flag per field. The learning protocol (R12-033) declares which flags are set.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Baselines and scoring
gap_vars.name: Real vs nominal dollars
gap_vars.description: Whether fares, costs and profits from scenarios in different years are converted to one price year before scores are pooled.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Options: nominal / deflated to a base year with CPI-U (New York-Newark-Jersey City) / normalised per scenario only (R12-057). NY-area CPI-U rose about 20% from 2019 to 2024 (2019 annual 278.2; 2024 mean of monthly values 334.2). The US city average rose about 23% [U]. TLC pay factors are re-indexed each March by NY-NJ-PA CPI-W (R07-028).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] BLS monthly NY-area CPI values for 2024 via search snippets. [uncertain: the 2019 annual average is from memory; bls.gov was not read]. [P*, from list] R07-028 indexation. [corrected: the ~23% figure is the US average, not the NY-area index].

gap_vars.how_to_model: Deflator table by month. The ledger stores both nominal and real values; the headline uses real values whenever eras are pooled.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Information level and the public vs insider line
gap_vars.name: Agent-visible history consistent with the sim's demand
gap_vars.description: Whether the historical summaries shown to the agent are raw TLC numbers, or come from the same pipeline (censoring uplift, smoothing, era) that generates the sim's demand.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Options: raw TLC aggregates / pipeline-consistent aggregates from non-test days (default) / the generator's exact rates (unrealistically perfect, close to an oracle) [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] R05-001 lifts demand for unserved trips (R05-066), while R12-014 serves summaries of past trips.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records
gap_vars.how_to_model: Compute the agent's history by running the sim's demand generator on held-out days, or apply the same uplift and smoothing to raw data. Log which version each arm uses.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Run validity (new sub-box)
gap_vars.name: Simulator correctness checks
gap_vars.description: Automatic invariant checks in every run: each car is in exactly one state, each request is served at most once, nothing changes the past, energy is never negative, and the money ledger balances.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Invariants: rider payment = driver pay + platform take + taxes, fees and pass-throughs (to the cent); car-state conservation; request life cycle; monotone clock. Checked on every event in development and every 1,000 events in evaluation [design]. Any violation voids the run.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] R07-015 and R07-066 define ledgers but no balance checks.
gap_vars.data_source: none needed
gap_vars.how_to_model: Assertion layer in the event loop, end-of-run ledger reconciliation, and property-based tests in CI.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Run validity (new sub-box)
gap_vars.name: Handling API failures and run validity
gap_vars.description: What happens on API timeouts, 5xx errors, rate limits, refusals or truncated outputs: how many retries, whether the sim clock keeps running, and when a run is voided rather than scored.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 3 retries with backoff. The sim clock is frozen during infrastructure errors (headline track) or charged (latency track). Refusals and truncations count as model behaviour (no-op). Void and re-run on the same seed if more than 2% of calls fail for infrastructure reasons [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]. [P, from list] Runs take hours of wall-clock time under provider rate limits (R12-065), and the serving provider changed Vending-Bench scores (R12-002).
gap_vars.data_source: none needed
gap_vars.how_to_model: A harness wrapper classifies each error as infrastructure or model, retries infrastructure errors with the clock frozen, logs counts, and voids runs above the threshold (malformed actions stay in R12-029).

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark and information / Visualisation and logging (reproducibility)
gap_vars.name: Benchmark version freeze and re-scoring rule
gap_vars.description: Simulator code, calibrated parameters, data snapshot and rule tables are versioned together. Scores are compared only within a version, and older models are re-run after an upgrade.
gap_vars.values_or_range: A version number per release (v1.0, v1.1, ...). Major bump on any calibration or rule change. Re-run the top-k models on each major release. The leaderboard shows the version [design].

gap_vars.data_source: none needed

gap_vars.sub_box: R01 Geography and network / Zones and service areas
gap_vars.name: ODD connectivity: fleet islands across river crossings
gap_vars.description: Whether the robotaxi may use the bridges and tunnels that join parts of its service area; if not, the fleet splits into sub-fleets that cannot rebalance into each other. Rivers make this acute in NYC; it generalises to any geofence with chokepoints.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Per-crossing whitelist (e.g. Brooklyn Bridge, Manhattan Bridge, Hugh Carey Tunnel). Waymo's 2025-26 NYC test area was two pieces: Manhattan south of 112th St plus Downtown Brooklyn. Testing ended when the permits lapsed on 31 Mar 2026. Options: separate islands / bridges only / all crossings. Tunnels cut GNSS and cellular signal [U].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S, from list] Test area in R01-008 and permit lapse in R07-059; [S] Streetsblog and Bloomberg (Apr 2026): testing halted. [design] Cross-river trip shares come from the TLC OD matrix.
gap_vars.data_source: TLC OD matrix; Vital City waymo-map https://github.com/vitalcity-nyc/waymo-map ; OSM bridge and tunnel tags
gap_vars.how_to_model: Edge mask on crossings per vehicle type, with zones split into connected components. Cross-component requests are rejected or handed to a partner, and each component needs its own depot and chargers.

gap_vars.sub_box: R09 Driver (human) / I. Robotaxi: what replaces the human
gap_vars.name: AV capability transfer factor (Phoenix/SF to NYC)
gap_vars.description: One reported scenario knob that scales every AV parameter borrowed from today's robotaxi cities to NYC density: speed penalty, remote-assistance rate, stuck and incident rates, pickup failures and weather limits.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Presets low / mid / high: remote-assist rate x1 / x2 / x4 the Phoenix/SF base; speed factor 0.95 / 0.85 / 0.70; stuck rate x1 / x3 / x10 [design]. No driverless service has run in NYC. The test fleet was 8 cars with safety drivers; city and state permits expired on 31 Mar 2026, and the city had not renewed them by mid-2026.

gap_vars.data_source: none found (no NYC driverless data); CPUC and CA DMV AV reports as the base [U]

gap_vars.sub_box: R10 Traffic and travel time / Signals, grid and turn rules
gap_vars.name: Pedestrians and drivers exploiting AV deference
gap_vars.description: Pedestrians cross, and drivers cut in, more freely in front of a car they know will always yield, so robotaxis are slowed most where foot traffic is heaviest.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Extra AV delay per turn or curb pull = k x pedestrian volume x AV recognisability; 0-60 s per turn at Midtown peaks [design]. Grows with the AV share of traffic.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Millard-Ball (2018), 'Pedestrians, autonomous vehicles, and cities', J. Planning Education and Research 38(1), doi 10.1177/0739456X16675674: a game-theory model of 'crosswalk chicken' in which pedestrians gain impunity against cautious AVs (eScholarship PDF not read). Driver cut-ins and all magnitudes are [design]. [P, from list] NYC DOT pedestrian counts (R01-034) to scale it.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC DOT Bi-Annual Pedestrian Counts (NYC Open Data, R01-034); none found for AV-specific delay
gap_vars.how_to_model: AV multiplier on R10-019 turning delay and R10-037 curb search, keyed to zone-hour pedestrian volume.

gap_vars.name: Emergency-vehicle encounters and first-responder scenes

The counts are self-reported and probably low. Delay 1-10 min per stalled encounter [design]. Encounter rate by zone from NYC EMS and fire dispatch counts.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Mission Local (Aug and Nov 2023) and Axios/SF Chronicle via snippets. [corrected: '55 from Jan to Aug' -> logged by 8 Aug, mostly since May]. NYC rates are [design].

gap_vars.data_source: NYC Open Data EMS Incident Dispatch Data https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Public-Safety/EMS-Incident-Dispatch-Data/76xm-jjuj ; Fire Incident Dispatch Data https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Public-Safety/Fire-Incident-Dispatch-Data/8m42-w767 (both confirmed in the data.gov catalog [S])

gap_vars.name: AV stopping policy: brief in-lane stop vs strict legal curb
gap_vars.description: Whether the robotaxi may stop briefly in a travel lane or beside parked cars to load, as NYC drivers routinely do, or must find a legal curb gap (placement rule in R01-033).
gap_vars.values_or_range: Toggle: strict legal curb / brief in-lane stop of 60 s or less / human-like. Extra Midtown pickup time 0-3 min under strict vs about 0 human-like [design], with a fine and complaint hazard in the lax modes. Taxis and FHVs may stop briefly where standing is banned, within 12 in of the curb (34 RCNY 4-11(c)).

[S] In San Francisco, Waymo cars got 589 parking tickets in 2024 (74 for double parking, 124-134 for obstructing traffic) and about 4,200 in 2025, clustered at busy pickup spots (Jalopnik, Electrek, SF Gazetteer via snippets). [corrected: upgraded from U].

gap_vars.name: Depot siting constraints: zoning, permits, lead time, community friction
gap_vars.description: Where a depot may legally go, how long its chargers take to be energised, and neighbour complaints that can cap depot size or hours. Extends R11-043 (depot siting and cost).

Neighbour complaints happen: Waymo cars honked at night in a SoMa, San Francisco lot (Aug 2024), and Waymo fixed this with a software update. A size or hours cap is [design]. Scenario input: a list of feasible sites with lead times.

gap_vars.name: Safety-incident trust shock and regulatory contagion
gap_vars.description: A publicised robotaxi crash or failure, in the fleet or at a rival, that cuts rider demand for AVs and can bring regulator-ordered fleet caps or suspensions. The regulator side overlaps R11-060 and R08-060; the demand dip and contagion are new.

Fleet cap at 50%: after the 17 Aug 2023 fire-truck crash, the CA DMV had Cruise cut from about 400 cars to at most 50 by day and 150 at night. Full suspension: the DMV suspended Cruise's deployment and driverless testing permits on 24 Oct 2023. Chance of contagion to other operators 0-50% [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] SF Standard and InsideEVs (Aug 2023) on the 50%/50/150 cap; [S] TechCrunch (24 Oct 2023) on the suspension [upgraded from U]; [U] GM ended Cruise robotaxi funding (Dec 2024).
gap_vars.data_source: CA DMV press releases; NHTSA Standing General Order crash data https://www.nhtsa.gov/laws-regulations/standing-general-order-crash-reporting

(b) Join an accessible dispatcher that serves 90% of WAV requests within 10 min (35 RCNY 59B-17), for a fee per WAV request [design]. (c) A human WAV sub-fleet of k cars. gap_vars.name: Strength of the fallback autopilot between model calls
