gap_vars.values_or_range: Permit cost $0-50k per car-year [design]. The NYC AV test permit costs $5,000 a year (34 RCNY 4-17, from list). Taxi medallions peaked at about $1-1.3M around 2013-14, then collapsed (some sold for under $140k at a 2019 auction). FHV licence pause since 2018 (R06-053).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Medallion price history via press snippets [upgraded from U; peak widened to $1-1.3M]. [P*, from list] AV test permit fee.
gap_vars.data_source: 34 RCNY 4-17 via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive ; TLC medallion transfer data [U]
gap_vars.how_to_model: Permit cost per car-year in the fixed-cost stack, plus a growth cap per period for phased schemes.

gap_vars.sub_box: R11 Fleet level / B. Control architecture and information
gap_vars.name: Fleet-wide learning of closures and hazards
gap_vars.description: When one fleet car meets an unmapped closure or hazard, the map update reaches all cars, so only the first car pays the delay.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Propagation delay 0-30 min; 50-100% of later encounters avoided [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]; [U] operators describe pushing map updates fleet-wide.
gap_vars.data_source: none found
gap_vars.how_to_model: Shared closure memory in the fleet map. The R03-055 delay applies only to cars that meet the closure before the update. Compare N=1 with N=100.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / I. Destination value, stranding and airports
gap_vars.name: Landing-to-curb lag (deplaning, immigration, baggage)
gap_vars.description: The delay between a flight reaching the gate and its passengers requesting or hailing a ride, which is short for domestic flights and long and variable for international ones.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Domestic about 15-35 min after gate arrival [U]. International about 40-90+ min, of which the CBP passport queue is about 15-60+ min [S]. JFK: FlightQueue's estimate from historical CBP data is about 26 min for US citizens and 37-48 min for non-US citizens [S; corrected by fact-check: a third-party estimate, not an official CBP average]. Peaks run well over 1 h (a U.S. Travel Association report cited 4.5 h at JFK in Dec 2012) [S]. LGA is almost all domestic, JFK heavily international and EWR mixed [U]. This refines the flat 20-60 min release window in R05-062.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] FlightQueue estimate (above). [S] Global Gateway Alliance analysis of CBP data, reported Dec 2013: kiosks at JFK Terminal 4 cut the average wait from 34.9 to 16.6 min and the maximum from 97 to 58 min within a month of installation (Oct to Nov 2013; the blog's '2012' baseline date looks like a typo). Joining the queue at the scheduled landing of an international bank is about an hour early [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: all (airport pickups); taxi via the holding lot; fleet airport allocation (R11-024)
gap_vars.data_source: CBP Airport Wait Times https://awt.cbp.gov (hourly average and maximum waits by airport and terminal; host not reachable from this session) [U]. BTS On-Time Performance https://www.transtats.bts.gov/ gives gate-in times for domestic nonstop flights of reporting US carriers ONLY, so it misses all international arrivals [S, corrected by fact-check]. For international arrival times: airport flight-status pages or OpenSky Network ADS-B landing data [U]. PANYNJ monthly airport traffic reports give the domestic/international passenger split [U].
gap_vars.how_to_model: For each arriving flight, release requests at gate time plus a lognormal lag set by domestic/international and terminal, with the CBP part drawn from that hour's published wait. This replaces the fixed 20-60 min offset in R05-062. Generalises to any airport through its international share.

gap_vars.sub_box: R09 Driver (human) / C. Breaks and bodily needs
gap_vars.name: Breaks taken while waiting in an airport queue
gap_vars.description: Meals, prayers and restroom stops taken inside an airport holding lot overlap with queue time instead of adding to it, within the limits of each queue's place-keeping rules.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Share of queue time usable as break time 0-80% [design]. A 12 h driver needs about 60-90 min of breaks (R09-010). With one 90-min airport queue, overlapping 30-60 min of breaks cuts the queue's opportunity cost by a third or more [design]. App drivers keep their virtual-queue place only while online and inside the lot geofence (R06-042) [S], so walking to facilities outside the lot risks the place. Taxis: a driver may occupy a taxi stand for no more than 1 h on relief time (35 RCNY 80-19(d)(5)). At terminals with holding areas the driver must park in the holding area before taking relief and join the END of the Feed Line on return (80-19(e)(2)) [P*; added by fact-check], so a taxi break can cost queue position.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design] arithmetic above, mainly for drivers who use airport-queue strategies. [P*] 35 RCNY 80-19(d)(5) and (e)(2) (rule text re-read in a local copy of the jehiah/nyc_code_archive). [S] amNY and NBC NY (2016-17): the Port Authority said app drivers could use restrooms at the JFK central taxi hold, but drivers avoided leaving their lot for fear of losing their place in line; portable toilets were later added to the FHV lot. Food trucks and prayer space at the lots [U].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver, taxi (not robotaxi: no breaks, R09-044); human-driven fleet (break scheduling)
gap_vars.data_source: none found for usage shares; 35 RCNY 80-19 via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; lot amenities from PANYNJ and the Uber JFK driver page [U]
gap_vars.how_to_model: While the car holds a queue place in a lot with amenities, the agent may take a break that reduces hunger, bathroom and fatigue needs. App queue: the place is kept while the car stays online inside the geofence; a walk to off-lot facilities carries a small chance of a missed dispatch. Taxi queue: per 80-19(e)(2), a break taken from the holding area sends the cab to the end of the feed line if its turn came. Break minutes count toward R09-010 needs.

gap_vars.sub_box: R01 Geography / Curb access and restricted streets
gap_vars.name: Enforcement intensity and being moved on
gap_vars.description: The chance, by zone, hour and day, that traffic agents, NYPD or Port Authority police ticket or move on a car standing or double-parked while it waits near a hotspot.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Hazard per waiting minute about 0-5% by zone and hour [design]. Close to certain at airport terminal curbs and Midtown transit hubs at peaks [U]. Fines are $100-115 for No Standing or No Stopping (R08-053). Robotaxi: California AB 1777 (signed Sep 2024) lets police issue a 'notice of AV noncompliance' to the AV company from 1 Jul 2026; the company must send it to the DMV within 72 h, and penalties are left to DMV rules [S]. NYC has no AV ticketing rule [U].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] NYC Open Data 'Parking Violations Issued' (one dataset per fiscal year; FY2026 covers 1 Jul 2025 to 30 Jun 2026) records violation code, time, street and precinct for each ticket as issued, not later dismissals (data.gov catalog). Tickets measure enforcement; being moved on leaves no record, so its rate must be assumed [design]. Whether waiting near a hotspot pays depends on this. The list has fine amounts (R08-053) but no enforcement map [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver, taxi; robotaxi via curb dwell limits; fleet staging (R11-023)
gap_vars.data_source: NYC Open Data, Parking Violations Issued (one dataset per fiscal year since FY2014, e.g. https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/parking-violations-issued-fiscal-year-2026); NYC Open Parking & Camera Violations; curb lengths from NYC LION/CSCL street centrelines [U]
gap_vars.how_to_model: Fit a zone x hour x day-type hazard from standing, stopping and double-parking tickets per curb-km. Each waiting minute draws a move-on (the car must cruise) or a ticket (fine from R08-053), with the move-on to ticket ratio as a tuning knob. Generalises to any city with open ticket data.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Information level and the public vs insider line
gap_vars.name: Price-checking zones in the public rider app
gap_vars.description: Drivers open the public rider app to see the quoted price, pickup ETA and nearby car icons for a zone before deciding whether to move there.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Settings: off / quote plus ETA for any zone, 1-3 min stale with +/-10-20% noise / capped at N checks per hour [design]. Car icons on rider apps are approximate [U].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [U] described in driver guides and forums. It is a public, legal reading of local surge and supply that R12-019 (driver-app signals) does not cover [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; taxi (to read app competition); fleet operator (watching competitor prices)
gap_vars.data_source: none (generated from the simulator's own matching state)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Tool rider_quote(zone) returns a price multiplier and ETA from the sim state with delay, coarsening and noise. Each call costs simulated seconds and counts against the tool budget (R12-028).

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
gap_vars.name: Physical state carried from one day to the next
gap_vars.description: Which state beyond memory notes ends one day and starts the next: car position, fuel or charge, sleep debt and fatigue, the weekly TLC hour counter, the weekly lease already paid, quest progress, ratings, rest days and sick days.
gap_vars.values_or_range: A reset-or-carry flag for each variable. Candidates to carry: end position (a 4 am finish in Brooklyn means a late start), charge or fuel, sleep debt (under 7 h of sleep means a slower or shorter next shift [design]), the TLC 60 h Monday-Sunday counter (R09-005), weekly rental already paid (R08-033), weekly quests (R07-033), rating and acceptance windows (R09-039, R09-040), 0-1 rest days a week, and a 1-3% chance of a sick day [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P*] The weekly 60 h passenger-time cap in 35 RCNY 80-14(f) (via R09-005) only binds if hours carry across days. R12-033 covers only memory notes and R02-068 only where the day boundary falls [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: all; fleet (car positions, charge and maintenance counters carry overnight)
gap_vars.data_source: none needed (harness setting); rule inputs from R09-005, R08-033 and R07-033
gap_vars.how_to_model: A day-boundary function copies or resets each state variable according to the protocol arm. Report scores for both 'independent days' and 'chained days'.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / F. Pickup, boarding and hail encounter
gap_vars.name: Street hailers' direction bias (taxi)
gap_vars.description: Street hailers mostly flag cabs already heading their way, so the avenue and direction a cab cruises on shapes where its riders want to go.
gap_vars.values_or_range: On one-way avenues, 60-85% of hailers have a destination ahead of the cab [design guess]. The effect is weaker on two-way streets and at taxi stands.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [U] taxi-driver lore. TLC data is zone-level with no heading, so it can only partly test this. It matters most for steering toward home or the garage at shift end (R05-060) [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: taxi (street hail); not app cars or robotaxis
gap_vars.data_source: none found (TLC yellow records give pickup and drop-off zones only)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Condition each hail's destination on the cab's heading by tilting the R05-006 destination weights toward zones ahead of it on its one-way street.

gap_vars.sub_box: R10 Traffic and travel time / Bridges, tunnels and highways
gap_vars.name: HOV-lane eligibility when carrying riders
gap_vars.description: A car with enough riders aboard may use peak HOV lanes, while an empty car, and a robotaxi carrying a single rider, may not.
gap_vars.values_or_range: The LIE HOV lane in Nassau and Suffolk (about 40 miles [U]) is HOV-2+ on weekdays 6-10 am and 3-8 pm; a violation is a ticket of up to $150 and up to 2 licence points. The Clean Pass solo-EV exemption ended on 30 Sep 2025 [S]. Inside NYC the HOV lanes are HOV-3+: the LIE approach to the Midtown Tunnel in Queens (7-10 am), the Staten Island Expressway and the Gowanus Expressway, with hours varying by lane [S, 511NY page via search snippet; corrected by fact-check, was 'SIE and Gowanus HOV/bus lanes [U]']. So an app car or taxi with ONE rider (2 occupants) qualifies only on the Long Island HOV-2 lane, and inside the city needs 2+ riders. 511NY says Uber, Lyft and taxis may use HOV lanes when they meet the occupancy rule [S]. A robotaxi with one rider has one occupant and qualifies nowhere [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] PIX11, CBS New York and News 12 (2025) on the LIE HOV rule and the end of Clean Pass; [S] 511NY HOV page (snippet). It affects only peak Long Island trips and group rides on the SIE, Gowanus or Midtown Tunnel approach, a small part of the ~4% of trips that end out of the city (G2-031).
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver, taxi; robotaxi (not eligible with one rider); fleet (routing)
gap_vars.data_source: 511NY Rideshare HOV lane page https://511nyrideshare.org/hov-lanes (host not reachable from this session; snippet only); OpenStreetMap hov=* tags
gap_vars.how_to_model: Link speeds depend on occupancy: an HOV link is usable when occupants are at or above its threshold (2 or 3) and its time window is active, so loaded and empty cars get different travel times on the same road. Generalises to HOV/HOT lanes in LA, the Bay Area, etc.

gap_vars.sub_box: R03 Events / Venue events and the event calendar
gap_vars.name: Unlisted private events
gap_vars.description: Weddings, proms, quinceaneras, funerals and banquet-hall parties that no public calendar lists but that create local demand spikes, mostly on spring and summer Saturdays.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0-3% of Saturday-evening demand citywide, concentrated in zones with catering halls. Single spikes of 20-150 trips in one zone-hour [design guess].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design] These spikes are an irreducible floor of 'unexplained' demand. That floor limits how much event information can add in the with/without-info test (R03-060).
gap_vars.data_source: none found for events. NYS Liquor Authority 'Current Liquor Authority Active Licenses' on data.ny.gov (dataset 9s3h-dpkz, with licence type, so catering establishments can be located) [S]. Residual Saturday spikes in TLC data (method of R03-066).
gap_vars.how_to_model: Schedule small Poisson events at catering-hall zones (Saturday evenings, seasonal weights) using TLC residual templates. They never appear in any information arm.

gap_vars.sub_box: R01 Geography / Transit hubs and airports
gap_vars.name: Ferry terminals and heliports
gap_vars.description: Staten Island Ferry terminals, NYC Ferry and NY Waterway landings, and Manhattan heliports produce small, timed pulses of pickup demand.
gap_vars.values_or_range: The Staten Island Ferry runs 24/7, every 15-20 min at rush hours and at least every 30 min at other times (2015 city policy; cut to hourly during COVID, later restored to half-hourly) [S; corrected by fact-check, was 'every 15-60 min [U]']. NYC Ferry hourly boardings by landing are public [S]. Heliports: Downtown Manhattan (Pier 6), E 34th St, W 30th St [U]. Each arrival yields from a few to tens of pickups [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] The NYC Ferry Ridership dataset (t5n6-gx8c) gives hourly boardings by date, route, direction and landing. [S] Staten Island Ferry Ridership Counts (6eng-46dm) give daily riders at Whitehall and St. George. Whitehall late at night is a known taxi spot [U].
gap_vars.applies_to: all (taxi via hails and the stand at Whitehall)
gap_vars.data_source: NYC Ferry Ridership, NYC Open Data t5n6-gx8c https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/t5n6-gx8c; Staten Island Ferry Ridership Counts, NYC Open Data 6eng-46dm (daily; trip-level counts only in an NYC DOT folder) [S, corrected: was 'none found']; NYC Ferry and Staten Island Ferry GTFS [U]
gap_vars.how_to_model: Treat ferry landings and heliports as timed trip generators like rail hubs (R01-049): arrivals x riders per boat x car share, released 2-8 min after docking. Split Staten Island Ferry daily counts over boats with the schedule.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / E. Request attributes and special needs
gap_vars.name: Mid-trip destination changes and repricing
gap_vars.description: Riders change or mistype the destination or add stops after pickup, and the platform reprices the fare and driver pay on actual time and distance. Stops entered before the trip are R05-033.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 1-3% of app trips [design guess]. NYC-specific address traps include hyphenated Queens addresses and street names repeated across boroughs [U]. The 120% cap on the fare estimate does not apply when the passenger alters the route, including the destination, number of stops, vehicle type or a toll route (35 RCNY 59B-23, via R07-022) [P*, re-read by fact-check]. Taxi trips are metered, so they need no repricing.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59B-23 rule text; [U] Uber/Lyft help pages on fare adjustment. This weakens decisions based on the upfront offer (R06-025).
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver, robotaxi (rider edits in the app), fleet
gap_vars.data_source: none found (TLC data records only the final drop-off)
gap_vars.how_to_model: With a small probability per trip, redraw the destination mid-trip or add a stop. Recompute fare and pay on actual miles and minutes, and log the quote-vs-final gap.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / D. Price, wait and mode choice
gap_vars.name: Rider promotions and memberships on incumbent apps
gap_vars.description: Promo codes, Uber One and Lyft Pink memberships and corporate vouchers lower a rider's price on one app without changing driver pay, which shifts demand between apps.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Uber One gives 6% back in Uber Cash on rides (it replaced a 5% discount in 2023); Lyft Pink gives about 5% off rides; both cost $9.99/month [S]. Uber One reportedly had about 50M members accounting for over half of Uber gross bookings in Q1 2026 [S, secondary summary]. Short promotions of 5-20% off on one app for 1-7 days [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] TechCrunch (May 2023) on Uber One's switch to cash back; RideWise and Ridesharing Driver comparisons (2025-26); Briefing.com Q1 2026 summary. It matters for a multi-apping driver (R06-034) because it moves request share between apps while pay stays the same.
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver (multi-app), fleet on a platform
gap_vars.data_source: none found (platform pages only)
gap_vars.how_to_model: A time-limited multiplier on each app's demand share (R05-004) and on riders' price elasticity, with driver pay unchanged. Members get a standing 5-6% price cut on their home app.

gap_vars.sub_box: R09 Driver (human) / E. Motivation and labour supply
gap_vars.name: Payout timing and cash-flow pressure
gap_vars.description: Weekly payouts versus paid instant cash-outs, weekly rental due dates and ticket deductions from deposits put pressure on a driver's cash on hand.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Lyft Express Pay: $0.50 per transfer at launch, raised to $1.25 per The Rideshare Guy (year of change not shown) [S]. An unofficial 2026 fintech guide lists $1.75 and says the fee is waived in New York State [uncertain: not confirmed by Lyft or the TLC]. Uber Instant Pay fee [U]. Weekly payouts are free. Rental is due weekly on a fixed day (R08-033). Taxi owners may deduct parking and red-light camera tickets from the driver's deposit (35 RCNY 58-21(e)(2), via R08-053) [P*].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] The Rideshare Guy on the $1.25 Lyft Express Pay fee; [S] Joingerald guide (2026, unofficial). The fee itself is small and may be zero in NY, but a persona short of cash works longer and accepts worse trips [design].
gap_vars.data_source: none found (platform help pages only)
gap_vars.how_to_model: An optional persona with a cash balance, due dates and a penalty for missing rent, plus an instant cash-out action with a configurable fee (default 0 for NY, $1.25-1.75 elsewhere).

gap_vars.sub_box: R09 Driver (human) / J. Agent decisions (action space)
gap_vars.name: Car-based delivery as a fallback
gap_vars.description: Switching to food or package delivery apps during dead hours or lockouts, an outside option some NYC drivers use.
gap_vars.values_or_range: NYC minimum pay for app delivery workers (restaurant delivery since 2023, grocery added in 2026): $21.44/h from 1 Apr 2025 and $22.13/h from the first pay period on or after 1 Apr 2026 (a 3.2% inflation adjustment), before tips [S]. Whether the rate is per hour of trip time or of all logged-in time [uncertain: rule text not read]. The worker pays car costs [U]. Robotaxi analogue: Waymo with Uber Eats in Phoenix (earlier pilot) [U], and with DoorDash in Phoenix (multi-year pilot announced Oct 2025, about 315 sq mi, orders left in the trunk) [S].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] NYC DCWP minimum pay pages and the 2026 rate announcement; [S] TechCrunch (16 Oct 2025) on Waymo-DoorDash. Gives dead hours and lockouts (R06-054) a realistic outside option [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; robotaxi fleet (idle cars); not taxi
gap_vars.data_source: NYC DCWP Delivery Workers https://www.nyc.gov/site/dca/workers/workersrights/Delivery-Workers.page
gap_vars.how_to_model: Action switch_to_delivery(hours) pays a fallback hourly rate times a utilisation factor, minus car costs. The car takes no rides while switched.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / F. Pickup, boarding and hail encounter
gap_vars.name: Wrong-rider pickups at crowded curbs
gap_vars.description: At crowded let-outs and hubs a driver can pick up the wrong rider, or spend extra minutes finding the right one, unless PIN verification is used.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0.1-1% of pickups at crowded curbs, costing 2-10 min and sometimes an unpaid wrong trip [design]. Uber's optional PIN verification was shown in Sep 2019, piloted in 7 cities and rolled out to all US and Canada riders in Jan 2020; when it is on, a trip cannot start until the driver enters the PIN [S; corrected by fact-check, was 'since 2019 [U]']. Robotaxi: the rider unlocks the car in the app, so wrong-rider risk is near zero, but finding the car can take longer [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]; [S] Inverse and local news (Jan 2020) on the PIN rollout. R10-039 and R05-040 cover pin error and R10-040 covers curb queues, but none covers wrong-rider events.
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; robotaxi (finding the car)
gap_vars.data_source: none found
gap_vars.how_to_model: A mismatch probability that rises with the number of cars and riders at the pickup node (R10-040), set to zero for riders with PIN on. Each event adds delay, or an unpaid trip plus a rider cancellation.

gap_vars.sub_box: R09 Driver (human) / G. Personal safety, preferences and life constraints
gap_vars.name: Safety tools and suspensions after unfounded complaints
gap_vars.description: Dashcams, in-app audio recording and rider ID checks, weighed against the risk that an unfounded rider complaint suspends the account pending review.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0-0.5 suspensions per 1,000 trips, each lasting 1-14 days [design]; a recording shortens them [U]. NYC L.L. 52 of 2026 (from 28 Jul 2026) treats restrictions of 72 h or more in a row as deactivations, which need just cause (via R07-045) [P*].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P*] NYC Admin Code 20-1281 to 20-1290 (via R07-045); [U] Uber/Lyft safety feature pages; [S] R09-043: 99% of Uber NYC deactivations are compliance-related.
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver; taxi (TLC complaint process)
gap_vars.data_source: none found for complaint rates
gap_vars.how_to_model: A rare per-trip suspension event, more likely at night [design], that removes days in multi-day runs; from 28 Jul 2026 NYC suspensions over 72 h follow the just-cause process. A dashcam option costs about $100-300 once [U] and halves the suspension length [design].

gap_vars.sub_box: R10 Traffic and travel time / Routing, navigation, GPS and ETA
gap_vars.name: Driver phone reliability and signal dead zones
gap_vars.description: Phones overheating on summer dashboards, battery drain, lost signal in tunnels and under elevated tracks, and app freezes cause missed or timed-out offers.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0-2% chance of missing an offer, higher in hot sun above about 30 C and in tunnels and under elevated tracks [design]. A second phone for multi-apping doubles the exposure [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [U] driver-forum reports. Missed offers hurt the acceptance rate (R09-040) and can lose an airport queue place (R06-042). R03-045 covers only network-wide outages.
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver, taxi e-hail; robotaxi connectivity drop-outs are R03-056
gap_vars.data_source: none found (carrier coverage maps are a weak proxy [U])
gap_vars.how_to_model: An offer-delivery failure hazard set by temperature (R04-019) and link type (tunnel, under elevated track); a failure counts as a timeout.

gap_vars.sub_box: R02 Time patterns / G. Institutional calendars and shift schedules
gap_vars.name: Taxi refuelling before shift handover
gap_vars.description: Yellow-cab drivers on driver-pays leases customarily hand the cab back with a full tank, so gas stations near the Queens garages queue up in the late afternoon.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Refuel stop of 10-25 min including the queue, between 15:30 and 17:00 [design]. If the owner supplies gasoline under the optional gas-surcharge lease ($13-31 per shift, set by the EIA New York City gasoline price index), the driver pays no fuel and does not refuel before handover (35 RCNY 58-21(c)(6)) [P*, added by fact-check]. Hybrids need about one fill per 1-2 shifts (R08-012) [design]. It deepens the 4-5 pm taxi supply dip (R02-044, R06-018).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [U] full-tank custom, which is not in 35 RCNY 58-21; that rule only provides the optional owner-supplied gas surcharge [P*, re-read]. [S] A 2011 TLC count found cabs on the road fell from 6,688 to 5,452 between 4 and 5 pm (via R02-044).
gap_vars.applies_to: taxi (day-shift lease drivers); competitor taxi bots
gap_vars.data_source: 35 RCNY 58-21 via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; OpenStreetMap amenity=fuel near garage zones; none found for queue times
gap_vars.how_to_model: A lease-type flag: gas-included (no refuelling) or driver-pays (must refuel before handover when the tank is below a threshold). Competitor taxi bots on driver-pays leases leave service 20-40 min earlier.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / D. Price, wait and mode choice
gap_vars.name: Riders who defer during surge and request again
gap_vars.description: Some riders who balk at a surge price postpone the trip rather than drop it and check again 5-30 minutes later, so demand returns as the price falls.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Of riders who balk at a surge quote, 20-60% defer, and 40-80% of those request again within 5-30 min [design guess]. Lyft's CEO said Wait & Save (cheaper in exchange for a longer wait) was about 30% of Lyft rides in Q1 2023 [S]. Lyft said NYC averaged more than 150,000 Wait & Save rides a week in Q2 2023 [S], roughly 13% of Lyft's ~1.1M weekly NYC trips (4.90M Lyft trips in Jan 2023 HVFHV data) [design calc; added by fact-check]. So many riders trade time for price.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] FOX Business interview with Lyft CEO Risher (no primary filing found) and Lyft Q2 2023 earnings call. Deferral flattens and lengthens peaks, so arriving 'late' to a fading surge can still pay; R05-020 treats every lost request as gone [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver, robotaxi, fleet (own pricing, G2-026)
gap_vars.data_source: none found (TLC records hold completed trips only)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Balked requests go into a deferral pool and come back over 5-30 min, re-quoted at the price at that time. Calibrate together with R05-020 and R05-066.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / J. Latent demand and demand feedback
gap_vars.name: Re-requests and duplicate requests
gap_vars.description: Whether a rider who is not matched, or whose driver cancels, requests again on the same or another app, and whether one person can hold requests on two apps at once.
gap_vars.values_or_range: After a failed match or a driver cancellation: 40-70% request again on the same app within 5 min, 10-30% switch app, the rest leave [design]. Requests open on two apps at once: 5-15% at peaks [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P*] HVFHV files hold completed trips only, with no failed or cancelled requests (R05-066); [S] rider multi-homing (R05-023). Without this, the censoring uplift counts some people twice [design].
gap_vars.data_source: none found
gap_vars.how_to_model: Riders persist after a failure, with probabilities of requesting again or switching app. When a duplicate request is matched on one app, the other app's request is cancelled, which shows up there as a rider cancellation.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Data pipeline and calibration
gap_vars.name: Double-counting guard for replayed days
gap_vars.description: Weather, event, holiday and disruption modifiers apply only to a baseline with those effects removed, never on top of a replayed real day that already contains them.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Rule: a replayed day gets no modifiers, or only the difference between the scenario and what actually happened. A synthetic day gets a baseline cleaned of weather, events, holidays and outages, plus modifiers [design]. Reference days used to build baselines must be screened for data gaps (R02-065).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own re-check on local yellow 2023 files. Replayed days already contain their shocks: on the 29 Sep 2023 flood day, yellow trips were +10% to +21% from 05:00-09:00 and -17% to -28% from 11:00-15:00 against 8 and 15 Sep and 6 and 13 Oct (day total -12%). [Corrected by fact-check: the +46-63% copied from R04-003 is very likely an artefact of using 22 Sep 2023 as a reference Friday. That day holds only 4,633 trips because of the TLC file gap (R02-065); with it in the reference set the morning shows +44-59%.] This is also a live example of a contaminated baseline. R03-066 removes only events from the baseline [design].
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records; NOAA weather; event calendars (R03); MTA alerts
gap_vars.how_to_model: Fit a de-shocked baseline by regressing zone-hour demand on weather, event, holiday, outage and data-gap indicators, and add scenario modifiers only to that baseline. A unit test checks that a modifier is never applied on top of a replay that already contains it.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Data pipeline and calibration
gap_vars.name: Demand timestamp basis (request vs pickup time)
gap_vars.description: Whether demand is fitted on request time (app trips only) or pickup time (all trips; yellow taxis have no request time), and how taxi demand is shifted back to request time.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023: request-to-pickup median 3.85 min and p90 7.92 min (Uber 3.72/7.42, Lyft 4.22/9.80). Binned by request time instead of pickup time, 30.6% of trips fall in a different 15-min bin and 7.7% in a different hour [P, re-verified exactly by fact-check]. on_scene_datetime is filled for 13.59M of 18.48M trips, essentially Uber only [P]. Yellow has no request time: street hails are close to pickup time, and e-hails need an imputed wait [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own re-check on the local HVFHV Jan 2023 file (18,479,031 trips, request_datetime filled for all). Fitting on pickup time moves let-out waves and rush peaks later by the wait.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime, on_scene_datetime, pickup_datetime) https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
gap_vars.how_to_model: Fit app demand on request_datetime; for yellow, use pickup time for hails. Check that simulated waits reproduce the observed pickup-time profile.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / C. Trip purpose and rider segments
gap_vars.name: Persistent rider population across days
gap_vars.description: Whether riders are fresh random draws each day or a synthetic population with home and work anchors, repeat commutes and stable traits such as tipping, no-shows and rating.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Fresh draws (default) / a synthetic population in which 20-50% of weekday commute trips repeat [design]; a stable tipper type (R05-047).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design] It gives the 10-day learning protocol regular patterns to learn and makes rating or blocking riders (R09-065) meaningful. R05-047 already assumes a persistent tipper type.
gap_vars.data_source: US Census LEHD LODES home-work flows https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/ [U]; NYC Citywide Mobility Survey [U]; TLC records (no rider IDs)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Generate a rider pool per zone with home and work anchors and traits. Each day's demand samples trips from the pool and matches the R05-001 totals.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / A. Trip generation volume
gap_vars.name: Within-day persistence and spatial correlation of demand shocks
gap_vars.description: How much a zone's demand deviation carries over from hour to hour within a day and is shared with nearby zones, on top of the citywide day factor.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023 non-holiday weekdays, zone-hours averaging 20+ trips: a date x hour factor explains 41% of the log-residual variance (0.050 to 0.030), and borough x date x hour explains 48%. The remaining zone residual has autocorrelation 0.35-0.36 at 1 h, 0.28 at 2 h, 0.22-0.23 at 3 h and 0.11-0.13 at 6 h [P, replicated by fact-check]. Poisson noise is about 58-62% of that residual variance, so the underlying shock persists more: about 0.85-0.9 at 1 h, about 0.55 at 3 h and about 0.3 at 6 h [design inference]. Morning (7-10 h) and evening (16-19 h) residuals of the same zone-day correlate 0.22-0.23 [P].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own re-check on the local HVFHV Jan 2023 file (the critic's method gave 0.40 at 1 h and 0.26 at 3 h; the fact-check's complete-grid version gave 0.35 and 0.22). Persistent shocks are what make watching the first hours worthwhile; R05-002 keeps one zone multiplier per day.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (pickups by zone, date and hour)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Zone log-multiplier follows an hourly AR(1) process with rho about 0.8-0.85, optionally plus a small zone-day component, a borough x day x hour factor and the citywide day factor, with Poisson arrivals. [Corrected by fact-check: a pure AR(1) at 0.85-0.9 implies 0.61-0.73 at 3 h and 0.38-0.53 at 6 h, above the ~0.55 and ~0.3 implied by the data.] Validate against the autocorrelations above.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Data pipeline and calibration
gap_vars.name: Population sampling fraction and density scaling
gap_vars.description: Whether the simulator runs all riders and background cars in the agent's area or only a sample, and if a sample, how the matching radius, queues and road capacity are rescaled.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 100% / 25% / 10% sample [design]. With cars placed at random, the distance to the nearest idle car scales with 1/sqrt(density), so a 10% sample gives about 3.2x longer pickups unless rescaled. Real data are much flatter across places: across weekday zone-hours, the elasticity of the median Uber on-scene ETA to trips per hour is about -0.03 to -0.10 depending on controls (pooled -0.08, within hour of day -0.09, within borough x hour -0.03) [P]. The median of zone-hour medians is about 3.3-3.9 min on Staten Island vs 2.0-2.3 min in Manhattan, depending on the minimum-trips filter [P; corrected by fact-check, was 3.45 vs 2.12, which is one filter choice]. Within the same zone and hour of day, busier days have LONGER waits (elasticity about +0.2), because demand shocks drain idle cars [P, added by fact-check].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on HVFHV Jan 2023 weekdays, Uber trips (on-scene time is filled for Uber rows only). [S] Frechette, Lizzeri & Salz 2019 (AER 109(8)): increasing returns in taxi matching (via R05-042). [U] MATSim rescales flow and storage capacity for sampled runs. R11-068 covers runtime only. The cross-sectional slope mixes density with supply response, so it is a calibration target, not a causal density law.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime and on_scene_datetime; Uber rows only)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Prefer full density in the agent's region. If sampling, shrink map distances by sqrt(f) or rescale the matcher. Require a calibration test showing that pickup ETA vs demand matches BOTH the cross-sectional TLC slope and the positive within-zone-hour slope.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Scenarios, seeds, difficulty and leakage
gap_vars.name: Tie-breaking and deterministic execution
gap_vars.description: A seeded rule for equal-ETA or simultaneous claims on one request, deterministic tie-breaks in batched assignment, and no dependence on thread order or floating-point quirks.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Tie rule: seeded random / rotate by seat / lowest car ID (to avoid) [design]. The same seed and the same actions must give an identical log [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design] Without it, the same seed does not reproduce a run and arena seats (R12-049) get hidden advantages. It affects ranking reliability and common random numbers (R12-040) rather than expected profit.
gap_vars.data_source: none needed (harness rule)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Resolve ties with a seeded draw per request from a dedicated random stream, iterate in sorted order everywhere, and have a CI test re-run a seed and diff the event log.

gap_vars.sub_box: R11 Fleet level / H. Market impact and service obligations
gap_vars.name: Fleet own-app pricing policy
gap_vars.description: In own-app robotaxi or fleet mode, whether and how the model sets its own fares, surge rules, caps, discounts and subscription price instead of accepting platform prices.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Off (default: platform or fixed rate card) / zone-hour multiplier of 0.7-2.0x with emergency caps (R04-012) / full rate card (base, per mile, per minute) / subscription price [design]. Reference: Waymo SF about $9.52 + $1.66/mi + $0.30/min (R07-061) [S]. Waymo Premier is an invite-only $29.99/month membership (launched Jun 2026 in SF, LA and Phoenix) with priority pickups and 10% back in Waymo Cash [S, detail added by fact-check]. NYC: HVFHS fares may not exceed the rate schedule filed with the TLC (35 RCNY 59D-17(a)), and final charges are capped at 1.2x the estimate (59B-23) [P*, re-read].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Castillo, Knoepfle & Weyl, 'Surge pricing solves the wild goose chase' (ACM EC 2017; tested on Uber Manhattan data); [S via list] Waymo rate card (R07-061). In the Uber-Waymo Austin/Atlanta set-up the operator has no price lever (R06-059), and Waymo Premier is not offered there [S].
gap_vars.applies_to: robotaxi fleet (own app), fleet with its own base; not single app drivers or metered taxis
gap_vars.data_source: Waymo pricing help page https://support.google.com/waymo/answer/9059184; 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive
gap_vars.how_to_model: Actions set_price(zone, hour, multiplier), set_rate_card(...) or set_membership(price, perks), bounded by the rule caps. Riders respond via R05-020 and R05-027, deferral via G2-018, and competitors via G2-045.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Data pipeline and calibration
gap_vars.name: Leftover easy-profit gap (no-free-lunch check)
gap_vars.description: The largest allowed gap between the best simple fixed strategy, such as always waiting at zone X at hour Y, and the average background driver's net hourly earnings.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Target: the best fixed heuristic beats the median bot by no more than 10-15% in net $/h [design]. Real-world reference: across 20 non-holiday weekdays in Jan 2023, HVFHV driver pay per engaged hour stayed between $52.42 and $55.82 ($55.43-59.30 with tips) while daily trips ranged from 478k to 701k (r = -0.16) [P, re-verified exactly by fact-check].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own re-check on the local HVFHV Jan 2023 file; [S] Buchholz 2022 (REStud) on the spatial equilibrium of NYC taxi search; [S] Hall, Horton & Knoepfle 2023 (NBER w30883) on re-equilibration (via R06-012).
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (driver_pay, tips, trip_time)
gap_vars.how_to_model: A CI test grid-searches simple fixed policies (zone x hour waits, always-airport) against the bots, and calibration fails if any beats the target margin persistently across seeds.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Data pipeline and calibration
gap_vars.name: Fare and pay engine validation
gap_vars.description: Recompute fare components and driver pay for replayed trips from the rule tables and the simulated route, and compare them with the recorded TLC fields against a threshold.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Target: median absolute error under 5% per trip for base fare and driver pay, and an exact match for fixed fees (congestion surcharge, airport fee, black car fund) [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] TLC files itemise fares (schemas re-read by fact-check from local 2023 files): HVFHV base_passenger_fare, tolls, bcf, sales_tax, congestion_surcharge, airport_fee, tips, driver_pay; yellow fare_amount, extra, mta_tax, tip_amount, tolls_amount, improvement_surcharge, congestion_surcharge, Airport_fee. R12-066 checks only pay per hour.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC yellow and HVFHV trip records
gap_vars.how_to_model: Run a sample of trips through the fare engine, using the rule vintage for the date (R07-065) and the simulated route. Report error by component and fail CI above the threshold.

gap_vars.sub_box: R10 Traffic and travel time / Travel-time engine and calibration
gap_vars.name: Same travel-time source for replayed and simulated trips
gap_vars.description: Whether replayed background trips use recorded durations while the agent's trips use the engine's travel times, and how the two are reconciled.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Engine times for all trips (default) / recorded times for all replayed trips / a hybrid that scales engine times to match recorded ones per origin-destination pair and hour [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design] Mixing sources gives the agent a built-in speed edge or handicap over the bots, and breaks the displacement rule (R06-067) when the agent takes a replayed trip. R06-066 does not say which source to use.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records (trip_time); NYC DOT Traffic Speeds https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/i4gi-tjb9
gap_vars.how_to_model: Every vehicle uses one travel-time function; replayed durations are used only for calibration (R10-062).

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Scenarios, seeds, difficulty and leakage
gap_vars.name: Warm-up and starting state of the background world
gap_vars.description: A burn-in period, or a start from replayed in-progress trips, so that bots, airport queues, open requests and surge are in a steady state when the agent starts.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Burn-in of 2-4 h of simulated time before the agent enters [design], or start from the trips in progress at t0 and historical airport queue lengths. JFK taxi holding-lot waits have been reported at about 2-3 h (R06-041, NBC New York) [S] [uncertain: R01-052 flags the figure as not re-checked].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design] Starting with empty queues and idle bots hands the agent free airport fares and easy offers in the first hours. R11-005 and R11-006 set only the agent's own fleet.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records (trips in progress at t0)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Run the world with bots only from t0 minus the burn-in, then insert the agent, checking queue lengths and idle shares against hour-of-day targets at that point.

gap_vars.sub_box: R01 Geography / Out-of-city trips and the empty return
gap_vars.name: Network extent and off-map trips
gap_vars.description: How far the road graph and travel-time model reach beyond the five boroughs, and how trips that end off the map are timed, located and returned.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023: 3.92% of trips end 'Outside of NYC' (zone 265; mean 16.6 mi and 34.4 min) and carry 10.4% of base fare; 0.63% end at EWR (17.2 mi, 39.1 min, 1.8% of fare) [P, re-verified exactly by fact-check]. Pickups from zone 265 are about 0.005% [P]. Zone 265 has no location, so the end point must be imputed from trip_miles and direction [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own calc on the local HVFHV Jan 2023 file: about 4.6% of trips and about 12% of base fare end off the NYC map. A fixed-time or instant-return shortcut misprices exactly these long trips; R01-057 gives only the share.
gap_vars.applies_to: all (taxi out-of-city rate codes; robotaxi only if the ODD allows)
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records (zone 265, trip_miles, trip_time); OpenStreetMap roads for NJ, Westchester, Nassau and Suffolk; NJDOT/NYSDOT speed data [U]
gap_vars.how_to_model: Extend the road graph to a buffer of about 50 km around NYC, impute the off-map drop-off point by matching trip_miles to county centroids, and route the empty return (R01-059).

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Baselines and scoring
gap_vars.name: Uncertain parameters and ranking stability
gap_vars.description: Run the leaderboard over a set of plausible draws of the guessed parameters and report whether model rankings hold, with each parameter tagged by where its value came from.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Parameters to vary: unserved demand 5-20% (R05-066), supply elasticity 0.2-1.0 (R06-010), price elasticity (R05-020), bot strategy mix (R06-017). Use 10-30 draws and report Kendall's tau of rankings across them [design]. Give wider ranges to values borrowed from SF, Chicago or pre-2019 studies.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design]; [U] domain randomisation (Tobin et al. 2017, IROS) is standard sim-to-real practice. If rankings flip within these ranges, the benchmark measures the guess, not the model.
gap_vars.data_source: none needed (harness setting)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Latin-hypercube draws over the flagged parameters, run first with cheap development models (R12-006), and a rank-stability panel published next to the headline score.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Baselines and scoring
gap_vars.name: Exploit and degenerate-strategy audit
gap_vars.description: A red-team pass with scripted probes and the RL baseline to find strategies that profit from simulator artefacts rather than real skill.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Checklist: free or instant repositioning, zone-centroid shortcuts, zero-time trips within one zone, farming cancellation fees, resetting queues by logging off and on, gaming the displacement rule, bots that never adapt, and loopholes in end-of-day valuation. Target: no probe beats the best honest heuristic by more than a few percent [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [U] specification-gaming examples (Krakovna et al., DeepMind blog 2020). R12-055 says RL shows 'how exploitable the world is', but there is no audit step.
gap_vars.data_source: none needed (harness setting)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Scripted exploit probes in CI plus periodic RL runs on development seeds; each exploit found becomes a regression test.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Scenarios, seeds, difficulty and leakage
gap_vars.name: Side-channel leakage audit
gap_vars.description: Checks that hidden state does not leak through the harness: sequential request IDs, wake-up triggers, error messages, tool latency, offer order, log timestamps, or heat maps built from the true hidden rates.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Pass or fail for each channel: random opaque IDs, wake-ups only on events the public could see, uniform error text, constant tool latency, and heat maps built from observed rather than true demand [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [design] Even with strict as-of rules (R12-022), a request-ID counter can reveal total demand, and an event-triggered wake-up can reveal an incident before the public would know.
gap_vars.data_source: none needed (harness setting)
gap_vars.how_to_model: An audit script compares what the agent sees across seeds that differ only in hidden state; any difference flags a leak.

gap_vars.sub_box: R12 Benchmark / Scenarios, seeds, difficulty and leakage
gap_vars.name: Checkpoint, resume and fork
gap_vars.description: Save the full simulator state, including the position of every random stream, so an interrupted run resumes identically and counterfactual branches can fork from the same mid-day state.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Checkpoint every 15-60 simulated minutes [design]. Fork arms such as with vs without event info, or alternative prompts, from one shared state.
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P* via list] Vending-Bench runs took 5-10 real hours (R12-065). Forking measures the value of information more precisely than rerunning whole days [design].
gap_vars.data_source: none needed (harness setting)
gap_vars.how_to_model: Serialise the world, agent memory, random-stream states and pending events. A resume test must give an identical log, and a fork API supports paired value-of-information tests (R12-061).

gap_vars.sub_box: R07 Pricing and regulation / I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
gap_vars.name: Geofence endpoint rule and boundary-trip leakage
gap_vars.description: Whether a robotaxi trip must start and end inside the service area, whether drop-offs just outside are allowed, and what happens to requests that cross the boundary.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Rules: both ends inside / pickup inside with drop-off up to X km outside / airport exceptions [design]. Proxy geofence: the TLC 'Yellow Zone' (55 Manhattan zones south of about E 96th and W 110th St, excluding Roosevelt Island) [P]. HVFHV Jan 2023: 30.5% of core pickups end outside the core. Trips with both ends inside are 24.5% of trips but 19.2% of base fare, vs 50.7% of fare for trips touching the core, so the strict rule keeps about 38% of core-touching fare. Yellow Oct 2023: 54.2% vs 87.2%, so it keeps about 62%, and only 10.7% of yellow core pickups end outside the core. Airport legs (JFK, LGA, EWR) are 16.7% (HVFHV) and 24.3% (yellow) of core-touching fare [P, all re-verified by fact-check].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P] Own re-check on local TLC files with the critic's geofence logic. [U] Waymo help pages and rider reports say pickup and drop-off must both be inside the service area. R01-008 and R07-060 never define the endpoint rule.
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records; taxi zone lookup (service_zone field) https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
gap_vars.how_to_model: Filter requests on (pickup zone, drop-off zone) by the rule. Rejected quotes lower rider retention (R05-068). Report the share of demand and fare lost.

gap_vars.sub_box: R11 Fleet level / C. Repositioning and rebalancing
gap_vars.name: Operator-chosen service area and request admission control
gap_vars.description: Inside the legal operating area, which zones, hours and trip types the fleet chooses to serve, such as a smaller area that keeps cars dense, refusing trips that strand cars, or capping trip length.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Actions set_service_area(zones, hours) and reject_if(trip_km > x or destination value < y) [design], bounded by coverage rules (R11-058) and, on human platforms, refusal rules (R07-042).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Cruise's first paid driverless rides in SF (June 2022) ran only from about 10 pm to 6 am on selected streets, with up to 30 cars, before expanding citywide in 2023 [upgraded by fact-check from U]. Waymo launches each city on a subset and then expands [U]. [S] Vazifeh et al. 2018 (Nature 557) on fleet size vs service level.
gap_vars.applies_to: robotaxi fleet; human fleet with its own base
gap_vars.data_source: NYC TLC trip records (to value zones); Waymo and Cruise service-area announcements [S]
gap_vars.how_to_model: Fleet-level masks on which requests the fleet will quote. Unquoted requests go to competitors, and the score includes coverage penalties.

gap_vars.sub_box: R08 Vehicle costs / Vehicle type, class and capacity
gap_vars.name: Per-vehicle autonomy capability (hardware/software generation)
gap_vars.description: Cars in one fleet may differ in what they can do autonomously, such as freeways, airports, snow or night driving, so some requests can go only to some cars.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Capability flags per car: freeway, airport curb, snow, heavy rain [design]. Example: Waymo's 5th-gen Jaguar I-Pace and 6th-gen 'Ojai' (Zeekr-built) cars in public service side by side since 28 May 2026 (SF, LA, Phoenix); about 300 Ojai in a fleet of 4,000+, and in Denver and San Diego (from Sep 2026) only the Ojai can be booked [S; updated by fact-check, was U]. Freeway rides were first offered to only some riders (R10-023) [S].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Electrive (May 2026) and CarNewsChina (Sep 2026) on the Ojai rollout; [S via list] R10-023 (freeway rollout) and R04-039 ('robotaxi generation' knob).
gap_vars.data_source: Waymo announcements [S]; none for NYC
gap_vars.how_to_model: Join a per-car capability mask to each request's requirements and to the route edge mask. This adds a matching constraint and a fleet-mix choice (R11-003).

gap_vars.sub_box: R11 Fleet level / I. Failure, risk and variance
gap_vars.name: Deliberate obstruction of robotaxis (coning, blocking, fake requests)
gap_vars.description: Interference that does no damage, such as cones on hoods, people standing in front of the car or fake requests that lure cars, but stops a car until remote help or a field team clears it.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0-0.5 events per 1,000 car-hours, higher near nightlife and protests, with 10-60 min of downtime each [design]. Safe Street Rebel's 'Week of Cone' in San Francisco was organised ahead of the 13 July 2023 CPUC meeting [S]; the group said it avoided bus routes and cars carrying passengers [S]. About a dozen cars coned [uncertain: count not found in sources checked].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] SF Standard and TechCrunch (July 2023) and NPR (28 Aug 2023): a cone on the hood shuts the car down until it is removed or a technician resets the car; Waymo called it vandalism. The cost is downtime and remote-assistance load, not repairs as with vandalism (R08-059).
gap_vars.data_source: none found (news only)
gap_vars.how_to_model: A hazard by zone, hour and event, applied only to empty cars if following the group's stated rule. Each event triggers a remote-assistance request (R09-048) and possibly field recovery (R09-050).

gap_vars.sub_box: R08 Vehicle costs / Energy use per mile and per hour
gap_vars.name: AV compute and sensor power draw
gap_vars.description: The constant electrical load of the autonomy computer, sensors, sensor cleaning and connectivity, drawn even while the car waits.
gap_vars.values_or_range: 0.5-2.5 kW continuous [U/design]. At city speeds, driving draws about 4-5.5 kW (0.3-0.45 kWh/mi at 12 mph; the Jaguar I-Pace is rated at about 0.44 kWh/mi [U]) [corrected by fact-check: was 0.25-0.3 kWh/mi and 3-4 kW], so this adds roughly 10-60% to energy per driving hour and far more while parked. 1.5 kW x 20 h = 30 kWh a day, a third of a 90 kWh pack [design]. The energy cost is only about $0.2-0.4 per hour at 1.5 kW [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Gawron et al. 2018 (Environmental Science & Technology 52(5)) and Gawron's 2019 University of Michigan thesis: Level-4 sensing and computing raise vehicle energy use and GHG emissions by 3-20% [citation corrected by fact-check]. [S] Sudhakar, Sze & Karaman 2023 (IEEE Micro 43(1)): onboard computing would need to stay under about 1.2 kW per car for fleet emissions to stay below 2018 data-centre emissions in most scenarios. The main profit effect is extra charging downtime, not the energy bill.
gap_vars.data_source: none public for Waymo; literature above
gap_vars.how_to_model: Add a per-hour kW draw to the EV energy model in every powered-on state (R08-008), so waiting drains range and drives charging (R11-035).

gap_vars.sub_box: R08 Vehicle costs / Energy prices and incentives
gap_vars.name: Utility managed-charging rewards and demand-response events
gap_vars.description: Utility payments for charging off-peak, and utility calls to cut charging during local grid peaks such as heat waves.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Con Edison SmartCharge Commercial (launched 14 Feb 2024) pays commercial and fleet charging sites for charging overnight and avoiding local peak hours, with a budget of up to $194M over three years [S, re-confirmed]. One listing shows it not accepting new applicants [uncertain: not confirmed]. Curtailment: 0-10 event days a summer, 2-4 h each, on heat-wave afternoons (R04-021) [design].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Con Edison press release (14 Feb 2024), Utility Dive and the EV Report. Curtailment can stop charging just when rider demand is also high. R08-020 and R11-039 cover tariffs, not incentives or events.
gap_vars.applies_to: robotaxi fleet; EV human drivers (SmartCharge New York for personal EVs)
gap_vars.data_source: Con Edison SmartCharge https://www.coned.com/smartcharge; NYISO load data https://www.nyiso.com/energy-market-operational-data [U]
gap_vars.how_to_model: A per-kWh rebate in off-peak windows, plus event days drawn from heat-wave days with a depot kW cap and a payment for compliance.

gap_vars.sub_box: R05 Rider demand / D. Price, wait and mode choice
gap_vars.name: Robotaxi adoption ramp and registered-rider base
gap_vars.description: How many riders have the app and will try a driverless car, growing over the weeks and months after launch through waitlists, word of mouth and novelty.
gap_vars.values_or_range: A logistic ramp with a launch-date parameter [design]. Waymo paid rides per week: about 50k (May 2024), 100k (Aug 2024), 200k (Feb 2025), 250k (Apr 2025), about 400k (Feb 2026) and 500k across 10 cities (Mar 2026), with a stated target of 1M by end-2026 [S; upgraded by fact-check from U]. Waymo opened SF to all riders in June 2024 after a waitlist [U].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] TechCrunch (Feb 2025; 27 Mar 2026), Sherwood News, CNBC/NBC on Alphabet's April 2025 earnings. Much of the growth came from new cities, so it is not a single-city ramp. In a new market, the number of signed-up riders, not the fleet, caps demand; R05-027 covers willingness to ride and the price premium, not the rider base.
gap_vars.data_source: Waymo company statements [S]; CPUC quarterly AV reports [U]
gap_vars.how_to_model: The share of riders eligible for robotaxi follows a logistic curve in time since launch and scales R05-004's robotaxi share for each scenario date, so demand grows in multi-day runs.

gap_vars.sub_box: R07 Pricing and regulation / I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
gap_vars.name: AV-specific road-use levies (per empty mile, per trip, displacement fund)
gap_vars.description: Fees a regulator could charge a robotaxi fleet per empty mile, per trip or per car, to curb empty cruising or to fund displaced drivers.
gap_vars.values_or_range: $0-0.50 per empty mile; $0-2.50 per AV trip; $0-5,000 per car-year [design]. A Jan 2021 report by Charles Komanoff for the NYC Council proposed charging app companies (not drivers) 11 cents per empty minute at peak, and half that at other times, in the zone south of 96th St [S]. The existing NYS congestion surcharge on FHV trips is $2.75 (R07-007) [S; tag downgraded by fact-check from P* to match R07-007]. The MTA congestion-zone charge of $1.50 per FHV trip (since Jan 2025) also applies [U, via R01-022].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] NYC Council press release and Streetsblog (Jan 2021) via R06-055. A per-empty-mile price changes the best repositioning and staging strategy far more than a cordon toll does [design]. This extends R06-055, which targets human app platforms.
gap_vars.applies_to: robotaxi fleet; human app fleet (the 2021 proposal's target)
gap_vars.data_source: none (scenario rule); NYC Council report https://council.nyc.gov/curbing-fhv-stockpiling
gap_vars.how_to_model: A scenario toggle that charges the fleet per empty mile or minute, per trip and per car-day; off by default.

gap_vars.sub_box: R07 Pricing and regulation / I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
gap_vars.name: Remote-operator location and licensing rules
gap_vars.description: Rules on where remote assistants must be based, what licence or training they need, and how many cars each may supervise.
gap_vars.values_or_range: An onshore requirement multiplies wages by 1-3x; a cap of 1 agent per 10-50 cars [design]. Waymo told Sen. Markey (Feb 2026) it has about 70 remote-assistance agents on duty for about 3,000 cars, about half in Arizona and Michigan and half in the Philippines (R09-049) [S, re-confirmed by fact-check].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Waymo's Senate Commerce testimony (4 Feb 2026) and letter to Sen. Markey (Reuters, Axios, TechSpot); Markey's 31 Mar 2026 follow-up found Waymo the only AV company using overseas remote operators and asked NHTSA to investigate [S].
gap_vars.data_source: Senate Commerce testimony and the Markey correspondence (via R09-049) [S]; none for NYC
gap_vars.how_to_model: A scenario rule that sets the remote-agent wage and the minimum ratio of agents to cars used in R11-052.

gap_vars.sub_box: R06 Supply and competition / B. Competitor driver behaviour
gap_vars.name: Incumbent platform response to the fleet
gap_vars.description: How Uber, Lyft and their drivers react when a fleet takes share, with targeted rider discounts, driver incentives or price cuts in the fleet's zones.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Competitor price cut of 0-5% per 10 points of share the fleet takes [design]. In San Francisco, Waymo's premium over Uber narrowed from about 31% (Mar-Apr 2025) to about 12.7% (Thanksgiving to New Year 2025, ~100k rides), cause unknown (R07-061) [S].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Obi price studies via TechCrunch (Jun 2025), Singularity Hub (Feb 2026) and Business Insider; primary Obi report not read. Holding competitor prices fixed overstates what a new entrant can win; R06-012 and R06-068 cover driver supply, not platform pricing.
gap_vars.data_source: Obi price reports [S]; none official
gap_vars.how_to_model: A competitor price multiplier in the fleet's zones responds, with a lag of days, to the fleet's recent share; off in single-car mode.

gap_vars.sub_box: R11 Fleet level / G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
gap_vars.name: Rider acquisition cost and promotions
gap_vars.description: Spending on first-ride credits, referral bonuses, promo codes and marketing to grow the fleet's own rider base.
gap_vars.values_or_range: $10-50 per rider acquired, plus a demand response to promotions [design]. Links to the adoption ramp (G2-042) and retention (R05-068).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Uber's FY2025 Form 10-K risk factors say driver incentives, consumer discounts and promotions have hurt and will keep hurting its financial performance. That they are booked as a reduction of revenue worth billions a year [uncertain: revenue note not read]. Leaving this cost out makes own-app profit look better than any real launch [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: robotaxi fleet (own app), fleet with its own base
gap_vars.data_source: Uber Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1543151/000154315126000015/uber-20251231.htm
gap_vars.how_to_model: Actions set_promo_budget(per day) or set_first_ride_credit($). Spending grows the registered-rider base and short-run demand, and the cost is booked against fleet profit.

gap_vars.sub_box: R11 Fleet level / G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
gap_vars.name: Fleet-level overhead and break-even fleet size
gap_vars.description: Costs that do not grow per car, such as an operations centre, a minimum 24/7 remote-assistance and field crew, licences, mapping and software, and the smallest fleet size that covers them.
gap_vars.values_or_range: HVFHS licence $190,000 a year (35 RCNY 59D-07(a)) and NYC AV test permit $5,000 a year (34 RCNY 4-17(c)) [P*, rule text re-read by fact-check]. One remote seat staffed 24/7 needs about 4.2-5 FTE (168 h / 40 h plus leave), so 5 seats need about 25 FTE [design]. Report break-even N on the scale ladder (R11-067).
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-07 and 34 RCNY 4-17(c) via R07-058. Charging fixed costs per car-day (R11-054) makes every fleet size look equally efficient [design].
gap_vars.data_source: 35 RCNY and 34 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive
gap_vars.how_to_model: A lump-sum daily overhead plus step costs (per remote seat, per depot) that do not depend on N. The score reports profit vs N and the break-even N.

gap_vars.sub_box: R11 Fleet level / F. Depots, maintenance and availability
gap_vars.name: Experience-curve cost decline
gap_vars.description: The remote-assistance rate, incident rate and mapping cost fall as the fleet's total miles in a city grow.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Cost = c0 x (cumulative miles / m0)^-b, with b = 0.1-0.3 [design]. Reference: Waymo's California miles per disengagement rose from about 5,100-5,600 (2016-17) to 11,017 (2018), 13,219 (2019) and 29,945 (2020) [S, added by fact-check].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] California DMV annual disengagement reports via Waymo's blog, VentureBeat and The Robot Report. These cover testing with safety drivers, not driverless remote-assistance rates, so they only roughly proxy the curve. Matters for multi-day and fleet-growth runs.
gap_vars.data_source: California DMV Disengagement Reports https://www.dmv.ca.gov/portal/vehicle-industry-services/autonomous-vehicles/disengagement-reports/
gap_vars.how_to_model: Track the fleet's cumulative miles per city and scale the R09-048 request rate and the R08-057 incident rate along the curve.

gap_vars.sub_box: R07 Pricing and regulation / C. App rider fares, surge and taxes
gap_vars.name: Flexible-ETA and priority ride tiers
gap_vars.description: Rider options to wait longer for a lower price, or to pay more for a faster pickup.
gap_vars.values_or_range: Wait-and-save: 10-25% off for a 10-20 min pickup window [design]. Lyft Wait & Save was about 30% of Lyft rides in Q1 2023 per the CEO, and NYC averaged 150k+ Wait & Save rides a week in Q2 2023 [S]. Uber Wait & Save was live in 10+ Indian cities (Jul 2025) [S]. Uber's priority option was tested at up to 20% above the basic fare in three Brazilian cities in 2021, and launched with a surcharge of unstated size in Buenos Aires, Mendoza and Córdoba in July 2023 [S; corrected by fact-check, was 'tested at up to 20% in Brazil and Argentina (2023)']. Waymo Premier ($29.99/month, Jun 2026) includes priority pickups [S].
gap_vars.impact_evidence: [S] Uber India newsroom (11 Jul 2025), Bloomberg (2021, Brazil), Argentine press (Jul 2023), FOX Business and Lyft Q2 2023 call. These tiers let a fleet batch trips and smooth peaks, which lowers the fleet size needed for a given service level [design].
gap_vars.applies_to: human app driver, robotaxi fleet (own app)
gap_vars.data_source: none found for NYC shares beyond Lyft's 150k/week
gap_vars.how_to_model: Each request carries a tier (standard, wait or priority) with a pickup-time window and a price factor; the matcher may hold wait-tier requests for batching.

top30.reason: Base request rate by zone and hour is the main input behind every dollar earned.
Pickup concentration: 16 of 263 zones give half of yellow pickups, so where you wait decides earnings.
Destination matrix sets where each trip leaves the car, and so the value of the next trip and the risk of stranding.
Weekday hourly demand curve (with R02-007 weekend) decides when working pays at all.
Competitor cars online by zone and hour set the ping rate and the agent's share of demand.
Matching algorithm decides which car gets each request, so positioning only pays through it.
Time-dependent link speeds set trips per hour and how per-minute vs per-mile pay adds up.
NYC minimum pay per mile (with R07-026 per minute) is the floor that sets app driver revenue per trip.
Surge raises pay where supply is short; chasing or ignoring it is a major strategic lever.
Taxi metered rate is the whole revenue formula for the taxi track.
Upfront offer information decides whether accept/decline is an informed choice or a gamble.
Repositioning to a target zone is the core geographic skill the benchmark measures.
Accept or decline: the per-offer choice that compounds over hundreds of offers per day.
Airport queue state: airports are 7.9% of yellow trips but 22% of revenue, against 2-3 hour waits.
Airport trip share and value: few, long, lucrative trips that dominate positioning trade-offs.
Rain demand uplift is the largest routine weather effect on app requests.
Event catalogue drives the event spikes and the with/without public-info experiment.
Information ladder defines what the model may know and how the value of each layer is measured.
Public vs insider boundary rule makes the comparison fair; break it and scores are meaningless.
Demand source mode (replay, resample, generator) sets realism, leakage risk and variance.
Supply elasticity: whether rivals react to surge and to the agent changes every payoff.
Latent vs observed demand: trip records show only served trips, which biases the base rate low where it matters.
Modifier composition and saturation: how hour x weather x event multipliers stack can blow demand up or flatten it.
Powertrain (electric vs gas) sets energy cost per mile, refuelling downtime and licence eligibility.
Cost accounting basis (marginal vs fixed costs) defines what 'profit' means in the score.
Wall-clock coupling: whether slow model answers cost sim time and missed offers.
Seeds and common random numbers make profit differences reflect decisions rather than luck.
Shift end and total hours: when and how long to work is the biggest single lever on daily profit.
Fleet size N sets the fleet level, market impact and self-cannibalisation.
Idle-car repositioning is the fleet positioning strategy the team wants to test.

still_missing: Driver taxes: after-tax profit (15.3% self-employment tax, IRS mileage deduction) has no variable of its own; it survives only as an optional note in R07-066, which is merged into R08-067.
Macro-economy and labour-market regime: in a recession more people drive for the apps and discretionary trips fall. No variable covers this; R02-033 only covers year-to-year drift in the data.
Public-health or pandemic shock scenario (a COVID-style demand collapse, rider limits, partition rules). It appears only as a data-era caveat.

Price of the main alternatives: subway and bus fares and fare changes (OMNY cap, fare-free bus pilots), LIRR/Metro-North CityTicket, and Citi Bike or e-scooter prices. R05-025 lists the modes but not what they cost.
Other ride-hail competitors are not named in supply: a Revel-style all-EV service with employee drivers, black-car bases, and outer-borough dollar vans (G1-013 may cover the vans).

Rider-matching preferences and anti-discrimination rules: women-rider preference features, and a ban on refusing or rating riders by neighbourhood, race or disability. Only the R12-059 scoring panel touches this.
Large groups split across several cars (one party requesting two or more cars instead of an XL), which changes how demand turns into requests.
Platform algorithm drift: pay or dispatch changes partway through the period, and pay personalised per driver. G1-001 covers how much pay varies per offer, not how it changes over time.

Local market power: the agent's share of idle supply in each zone and hour. R11-056 and R06-061 judge impact citywide, but surge and ETAs are set per zone, and 30-50 cars at a venue or airport can dominate it.

Own-app density economies: pickup ETA falls roughly with the square root of idle-car density, so profit per car can rise before saturation. R11-030 assumes a steady fall, and the N ladder {1, 10, 100} in R11-067 needs intermediate values.

One toll-liability rule for loaded, return and repositioning legs. It must reconcile R08-050 (the app rider pays the return toll on out-of-city trips) with R01-021 and R07-038 (empty-return tolls are unreimbursed). The driver's real cost is the deadhead time and energy back, plus tolls on voluntary repositioning.

Information footing of the baselines: R12-052 (OR planner) and any R12-051 heuristic that reads the generator's expected rates use insider information under R12-021. Give them the same L1/L2 data as the model, or label them semi-oracles.
Unserved-demand uplift as an explicit calibrated parameter (R05-066's '5-20%' design guess), varied in the G2-032 parameter-uncertainty runs and fitted on request_datetime per G2-021.

A single ODD object (polygon, hours, road classes, river crossings, weather limits, endpoint rule). The parts exist as R01-008, R07-060, R02-061, R04-039, R10-023, G2-036 and G1-038, but nothing ties them together.

Impact ratings to fix after the merges: weather speed effect (R04-008, which absorbs R10-006) should be medium (high in snow, low in rain). Cold-weather EV range (R08-010, which absorbs R04-037) should be medium. For the robotaxi track, the remote-assistance rate (R09-048) and pickup-point placement (R01-033) should be medium. R11-042's corrected 83-92% availability replaces the 75% in R09-044.
